The client verifies the server PID and refuses a reused target PID. The server also retains a SYNCHRONIZE handle to the controller process. A Windows thread-pool wait stops the worker if that process exits, including TerminateProcess; this expires the old pipe without Python close() or unloading the DLL. A new owner can attach to the same running AUT afterward. See SECURITY.md for the threat model.
  • Per-Qt-major-version DLL — Qt 5 and Qt 6 ABIs differ. We ship both, named dolphin_qt5_agent.dll and dolphin_qt6_agent.dll; the loader picks based on Application.qt_version().
  • Anti-cheat / DRM — apps that detect remote-thread injection (some games, banking apps) will reject the agent. There is no workaround short of cooperative integration.
  • Sandboxed apps — UWP / packaged apps with isolated containers cannot be injected without elevated privileges and AppContainer-aware tooling.

docs.title: Validation coverage
docs.text:
The required Qt5/Qt6 component suite includes six abrupt-owner-death scenarios: an authenticated idle connection, a disconnected transport waiting for reconnection, and an unfinished JSON frame, each with both Qt versions. The test checks a real authenticated ping, the actual controller PID, explicit Win32 TerminateProcess, its exit code, absence of Python cleanup, continued AUT liveness, stable disappearance of the old pipe and a new owner's successful attach/ping/introspection. These scenarios may not be skipped in CI.

Restricted-token and localhost-SMB tests remain controls for the local security boundary. They do not establish results for a second logged-in account or an independent remote machine. See the system isolation checklist for the remaining environment-dependent checks.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch_qt(f'"{sys.executable}" "examples/qt_demo/qml_widgets.py"')

# Triggers DLL injection + named-pipe connect on first access.
agent = app.qt_agent

# 1. Pure introspection
roots = agent.qml_root()          # list of QQuickWindow trees
btns = agent.find(className="QPushButton")

# 2. Property access
nf = agent.qml_find("qmlNameField")[0]["handle"]
agent.set_property(nf, "text", "Alice")
assert agent.get_property(nf, "text") == "Alice"

# 3. Method invocation (no-arg / typed args)
spin = agent.find(className="QSpinBox")[0]["handle"]
agent.invoke(spin, "setValue", 42)

# 4. QML click simulation (Qt event system, not OS mouse)
btn = agent.qml_find("qmlClickButton")[0]["handle"]
agent.qml_click(btn)

# 5. QGraphicsView walking
view = agent.find(className="QGraphicsView")[0]["handle"]
items = agent.graphics_items(view)
hit = agent.graphics_item_at(view, 60, 40)

The agent is closed automatically when Application.kill() / Application.close() is called. Use app.has_qt_agent() to check attachment without triggering injection.

docs.title: CI Setup
docs.text: Dolphin tests need Windows. The most reliable CI setup is an agent running as a logged-in user with access to an interactive desktop.

docs.title: Recommended Baseline
docs.text:
Start with visible mode:

python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[pytest]==0.2.0"
pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-backend=uia

Use dolphin-run only after you have verified that your target application and test actions work on a hidden Windows desktop:

dolphin-run pytest tests/smoke/ -v --dolphin-backend=uia

docs.title: Agent Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Reason Windows 10/11 or a prepared Windows Server 2022+ desktop session Dolphin depends on Windows UIA, Win32, and COM Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13 Package requirement Agent runs as a normal logged-in user UIA cannot drive another user's desktop Same privilege level as the app under test Non-elevated tests cannot automate elevated apps Artifact upload for traces/screenshots/videos Desktop failures are easier to debug visually

Avoid running desktop UI tests as SYSTEM unless you have a dedicated interactive-session setup and have verified UIA access with dolphin doctor.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
Useful options:

pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-screenshot-on-fail --dolphin-trace=on-failure
pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-video=keepfailedonly

Upload these directories when they exist:

  • dolphin-traces/
  • dolphin-videos/
  • dolphin-screenshots/
  • dolphin-report.html

docs.title: CI Guides
docs.text:
• GitHub Actions
  • Jenkins
  • TeamCity

See Headless Mode before using dolphin-run in a full suite.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text: Start with plain pytest on a Windows runner. Tests that send physical input or capture pixels require an unlocked interactive desktop and the target app's prerequisites. Verify those conditions for your runner image; use a prepared self-hosted desktop when the application or session cannot be provided by a hosted runner. See the full workflow example.

docs.title: Minimal Workflow
docs.text:
.github/workflows/tests.yml
name: Desktop Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: windows-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@ece7cb06caefa5fff74198d8649806c4678c61a1 # v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install
        run: python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[pytest]==0.2.0"

      - name: Check Dolphin environment
        run: dolphin doctor

      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-backend=uia

docs.title: Upload Failure Artifacts
docs.text:
- name: Install
        run: python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[fast,pytest]==0.2.0"

      - name: Run tests
        env:
          DOLPHIN_TRACE: on-failure
          DOLPHIN_VIDEO: keepfailedonly
        run: pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-screenshot-on-fail

      - name: Upload traces
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: dolphin-traces
          path: dolphin-traces/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload videos
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: dolphin-videos
          path: dolphin-videos/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload screenshots
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: dolphin-screenshots
          path: dolphin-screenshots/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

DOLPHIN_VIDEO above only produces MP4s if an ffmpeg binary is on the runner's PATH (or pointed at by DOLPHIN_FFMPEG). Without it, recording is skipped silently and the upload step finds nothing, so confirm ffmpeg is present on your runner image before relying on the videos. The fast extra installs mss for quicker trace screenshots; it does not encode video.

docs.title: Headless Smoke Job
docs.text:
Use dolphin-run only for tests you have verified on a hidden desktop:

  smoke-headless:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@ece7cb06caefa5fff74198d8649806c4678c61a1 # v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[pytest]==0.2.0"
      - run: dolphin-run pytest tests/smoke/ -v --dolphin-backend=uia

Read Headless Mode before moving a full suite to dolphin-run.

docs.title: Jenkins
docs.text: Run the Jenkins agent under a Windows user account that has an interactive desktop. Avoid running desktop UI tests as SYSTEM.

docs.title: Declarative Pipeline
Agent Checklist
docs.text:
• Windows 10/11 or a prepared Windows Server 2022+ desktop session.
  • Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13 in PATH.
  • Agent process runs as the same Windows user that owns the desktop.
  • Test process has the same elevation level as the application under test.

docs.title: Headless Smoke Tests
docs.text:
stage('Smoke on hidden desktop') {
    steps {
        bat 'dolphin-run pytest tests\\smoke -v --dolphin-backend=uia'
    }
}

Use this only for tests verified against the hidden-desktop limitations.

docs.title: TeamCity
docs.text: Run the TeamCity agent as a logged-in Windows user, not as SYSTEM, so UIA can access the desktop.

docs.title: Command Line Build Step
docs.text:
python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[pytest]==0.2.0"
dolphin doctor
pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-backend=uia --tb=short

docs.title: With Artifacts
docs.text:
python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[fast,pytest]==0.2.0"
set DOLPHIN_TRACE=on-failure
set DOLPHIN_VIDEO=keepfailedonly
pytest tests/ -v --dolphin-screenshot-on-fail --junitxml=test-results.xml

Artifact paths:

dolphin-traces/** => dolphin-traces.zip
dolphin-videos/** => dolphin-videos.zip
dolphin-screenshots/** => dolphin-screenshots.zip
dolphin-report.html
test-results.xml

DOLPHIN_VIDEO only produces MP4s when an ffmpeg binary is on the agent's PATH (or pointed at by DOLPHIN_FFMPEG); without it recording is skipped silently and dolphin-videos/** collects nothing. The fast extra installs mss for quicker trace screenshots — it does not encode video.

docs.title: Kotlin DSL Sketch
Headless Smoke Tests
docs.text:
dolphin-run pytest tests\smoke -v --dolphin-backend=uia

Use hidden-desktop execution only for tests that have been checked against the limitations in Headless Mode.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Use these guides after the quickstart when you know what kind of application you need to test.

Guide Start here when Native Windows Apps The app is Win32, WPF, WinForms, MFC, or VB6 Delphi / VCL and Lazarus The app is built with Delphi (RAD Studio) or Lazarus/LCL PowerBuilder The app is a PowerBuilder client (Appeon or classic) Electron The app is built with Electron or Chromium UI Embedded Web The app hosts web content (Electron, CEF, WebView2 overview) WebView2 The app embeds Microsoft Edge WebView2 CEF and Legacy IE The app embeds CEF or old Trident/MSHTML controls Java Swing / AWT The app is a Java desktop application Oracle Forms The app is an Oracle Forms client (Java applet / Web Start) Qt 5 / Qt 6 The app uses Qt widgets (financial, trading, KDE, AMD/NVIDIA control panels) IBM Mainframe The test drives a 3270 / 5250 terminal session or an HLLAPI emulator Office The test needs Excel, Word, PowerPoint or classic Outlook automation through COM SAP GUI for Windows The test targets classic SAP GUI with SAP GUI Scripting enabled Image-Based Fallback Accessibility APIs cannot see a rendered control Headless Mode You need to run tests on a hidden Windows desktop CI Setup You need artifact collection and Windows runner guidance

Prefer UIA or Win32 selectors when they are available. Use image matching only for controls that are not exposed through accessibility APIs.

docs.title: CEF And Legacy IE
docs.text: This guide covers applications that embed Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) or the legacy MSHTML/Trident browser engine.

docs.title: CEF
docs.text:
Start with UIA:

from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch_cef("MyCefApp.exe")
win = app.window(title_re=".*My CEF App.*")

launch_cef() appends --force-renderer-accessibility if the command does not already include it. Some applications ignore unknown command-line flags, so verify with:

dolphin spy --window "My CEF App" --depth 4

Detect CEF:

if app.is_cef():
    print("CEF detected")

docs.title: CEF Fallback
docs.text:
If the embedded content is custom-rendered or not exposed through UIA, the primary escape hatch for CEF's Chromium runtime is the CDP path — enable a remote debugging port and drive the DOM directly (see Embedded web). Use image matching only when a debug port cannot be enabled:

from dolphin_desktop import ImageLocator

submit = ImageLocator("templates/submit.png", threshold=0.9)
submit.wait_for(timeout=10)
submit.click()

Capture templates with:

dolphin spy --image-pick --output-dir templates

docs.title: Legacy IE / Trident (legacy, limited scope)
docs.text:
Older applications may host MSHTML through a WebBrowser control.

IE/Trident is not a separate DolphinDesktop backend or formal capability in the 0.2.0 Support Matrix; the Internet Explorer 11 shell is explicitly out-of-scope because the technology is end-of-life. The example below is a best-effort UIA/Win32 automation recipe for applications that still expose their embedded control. Application.is_legacy_ie() is a diagnostic detector, not a guarantee of supported DOM automation or a positive UAT claim.

from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch("LegacyPortal.exe")
win = app.window(title_re=".*Portal.*")

doc = win.get_by_role("Document")
doc.get_by_role("Edit", name="Username").type_text("admin")
doc.get_by_role("Button", name="Login").click()

Detect legacy IE:

if app.is_legacy_ie():
    print("MSHTML detected")

If UIA does not expose useful children, try the Win32 backend and class-name selectors:

desktop = Desktop(backend="win32")
app = desktop.launch("LegacyPortal.exe")
win = app.window(title_re=".*Portal.*")
win.get_by_class("Internet Explorer_Server").click()

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Prefer UIA or Win32 selectors when available.
  • Use image matching only for controls that accessibility APIs cannot see.
  • Test embedded browser apps in isolation; multiple similar windows can make broad selectors ambiguous.

docs.title: Delphi / VCL (and Lazarus / LCL)
docs.text: Dolphin drives controls exposed by the application's Windows UIA/MSAA tree. A Delphi compiler version does not guarantee that TForm.Name or TComponent.Name appears as UIA AutomationId. The earlier claim that VCL 10.4+ automatically provides this mapping was incorrect (KAN-761).

docs.title: Install and prerequisites
docs.text:
python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[pytest]==0.2.0"
  • Windows and a desktop session appropriate to the operations being tested.
  • The target must expose each required control and action through UIA. Inspect the actual target with dolphin spy --delphi --pid <pid>.
  • Lookup by Delphi Name requires an application-supplied UIA provider returning the exact TForm.Name / TComponent.Name as AutomationId on each required element. Setting Name in Object Inspector alone is insufficient. Verify both the form and its children; a provider on one does not cover all.
  • Dolphin supplies no VCL Name provider, injected RTTI agent, configuration switch or turnkey provider installation. Stock VCL Name lookup is outside the current support contract. Do not assume that upgrading Delphi enables it. Applications requiring it need a separately implemented and validated provider.
  • Stock Delphi 12 VCL exposed by official delphivcl==1.0.7 has an empty form AutomationId and numeric control IDs instead of component names. Its non-windowed TLabel may be absent from UIA entirely. A missing element cannot be recovered by name=, near_label= or switching to generic win32.

Official DelphiVCL bindings provide a real VCL runtime; a Lazarus sample is separate evidence and cannot establish Delphi VCL accessibility support.

docs.title: Quick start for UIA-visible controls
docs.text:
Choose selectors from the inspected application. For example, a known form with one Edit and a Save button can use:

from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

with Desktop().launch_delphi(r"C:\path\to\vcl_app.exe") as app:
    form = app.form(title="Customer details")
    form.wait_ready(timeout=10)
    form.component(cls="TEdit", index=0).set_text("Alice")
    form.component(cls="TButton", title="Save").click()

Indices depend on the target's tree order and captions on its language/state. This is a UIA workflow, not proof of lookup by Delphi Name. Only when an application's verified provider publishes MainForm, EdtName, and BtnSave as AutomationIds can the corresponding name= selectors resolve those IDs.

docs.title: DelphiApp
docs.text: Method Purpose form(name=None, title=None, title_re=None, timeout=15) Resolve a top-level TForm. name= matches a provider-published UIA AutomationId; use title= for captions. forms() Enumerate every top-level TForm in the process. application The underlying Application for teardown (app.application.detach() to opt out of pytest's PID reaper). close() / context manager Kill the app.

docs.title: DelphiForm
docs.text: Method Purpose component(name, cls=None, timeout=10) Resolve a child component. name = provider-published UIA ID (legacy caption fallback); cls is an optional Delphi class hint ("TButton", "TEdit"). components(cls=None) Enumerate UIA-visible descendant components, optionally filtered by class. wait_ready(timeout=15) Block until the form window is visible. title() Return the form caption. pywinauto Escape hatch — underlying pywinauto window wrapper.

docs.title: DelphiComponent
docs.text:
State reads: text(), is_visible(), is_enabled(), is_checked(), bounding_box(), lines(), items(), item_count(), cell(row=, col=).

Actions: click(), double_click(), right_click(), focus(), set_text(text), type_text(text, clear=True), toggle(), check(), uncheck(), select(item) (index or string).

Escape hatch: pywinauto returns the underlying pywinauto wrapper for advanced UIA calls dolphin does not expose.

docs.title: Selector resolution
docs.text:
app.form(name=...) queries UIA auto_id only. It does not read TForm.Name. title= and title_re= explicitly select window captions.

form.component(name=...) first queries UIA auto_id with a mapped UIA control type (if known), then without that type. For backward compatibility it also tries the same string as a caption, with type/class variants. A successful caption fallback does not prove component Name exposure. Prefer title= for intentional caption matching.

Explicit near_label=, index=, and title_re= strategies run before those criteria variants. near_label= requires an actual UIA-visible label, not a painted TLabel that is missing from the tree. components() enumerates the exposed UIA descendants; its .name is the published AutomationId or caption, not a read of Delphi RTTI.

docs.title: Reproducible real VCL reference
docs.text:
From the repository root, with the project development environment installed:

uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe delphivcl==1.0.7
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/delphi/test_real_vcl.py -q -o junit_family=xunit1 --junitxml=artifacts/vcl-reference.xml

The fixture tests/delphi/real_vcl_app.py uses the official runtime and assigns real component Names. It adds no UIA provider and injects no AutomationIds. The harness launches the Python host and attaches to the actual form-owning interpreter PID, since Windows venv launchers can create a child interpreter. The regression checks the actual tree and diagnostic errors for missing form, Edit and Button names. A separate reference workflow edits a real VCL Edit, invokes Save and verifies the resulting text using the supported UIA selectors. This separate workflow does not replace or pass DESKTOP-161's Name contract. DESKTOP-161 remains unsupported on this stock runtime without a real provider.

The test skips when the optional runtime is unavailable; a skip is incomplete real-VCL verification. Run on Windows with delphivcl==1.0.7. The LCL suite tests/delphi/test_sample_lcl.py independently validates Lazarus behavior.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check / action form(name="MainForm") or component(name="EdtName") fails Inspect UIA AutomationIds, not just Object Inspector. Empty/numeric IDs do not expose Delphi names. A provider is required for that contract. Component found but action fails Inspect supported UIA patterns, visibility and enabled state. Mouse fallback needs an interactive desktop. TLabel absent or near_label= fails Non-windowed controls can be missing from UIA. The application needs accessibility support for those controls. Grid cells are unavailable UIA exposure of the grid does not guarantee GridPattern or cell access. Verify the target's patterns. Third-party / owner-drawn control is invisible Support depends on its provider. Dolphin currently supplies no Delphi RTTI agent.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Support matrix
  • PowerBuilder
  • tests/delphi/sample_lcl/ — independent Lazarus sample

docs.title: Electron Apps
docs.text: Electron applications embed Chromium in a Windows desktop process. Dolphin can automate the parts of the UI that Electron exposes through Windows accessibility APIs.

docs.title: Launch With Accessibility Enabled
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch_electron(r"C:\Path\To\MyElectronApp.exe")
win = app.window(title_re=".*My Electron App.*")

launch_electron() appends --force-renderer-accessibility if the command does not already include it.

You can pass the flag yourself when needed:

app = desktop.launch(
    r"C:\Path\To\MyElectronApp.exe --force-renderer-accessibility",
    timeout=20,
)

docs.title: Detect Electron
docs.text:
if app.is_electron():
    print("Electron runtime detected")

Detection checks the Chromium window class and known Electron module names. It returns False on errors.

docs.title: Selectors
docs.text:
After accessibility is enabled, inspect the tree:

dolphin spy --window "My Electron App" --depth 4

Then use the exposed roles and names:

win.get_by_role("Edit", name="Username").type_text("admin")
win.get_by_role("Button", name="Sign in").click()
win.get_by_text("Welcome").wait_for(state="visible", timeout=10)

Not every Electron app exposes the same tree. Custom-rendered controls may require a different selector or an image fallback.

docs.title: App-Side Option
docs.text:
For an Electron app you own, enable the accessibility flag in test mode from the main process:

app.commandLine.appendSwitch("force-renderer-accessibility")

docs.title: Fallback
docs.text:
If a control is not visible through UIA, the primary escape hatch for Electron's Chromium runtime is the CDP path — launch or connect with a debug port and drive the DOM directly (see Embedded web). Use image matching only when a debug port cannot be enabled: capture a template and match on pixels:

dolphin spy --image-pick --output-dir templates

win.image("templates/sign_in.png", confidence=0.9).click()

docs.title: Embedded web apps — UIA, CDP fallback, Shadow DOM
docs.text:
Windows apps built on Chromium (Electron, CEF), WebView2, or Internet Explorer host web content inside a native shell. Two orthogonal problems show up when trying to automate them via UIA:

Case UIA reach Why Electron with --force-renderer-accessibility full DOM accessibility tree built on demand Electron without the flag (packaged apps) native frame only renderer never publishes an a11y tree Shadow DOM (any host) often hidden closed shadow roots are not exposed to platform a11y

Where UIA is blind, dolphin_desktop exposes a CDP fallback: attach to the Chromium runtime's Chrome DevTools Protocol port and drive the DOM directly. This section explains when to reach for it, how to install it, and what to expect.

docs.title: When to use CDP
docs.text:
Use CDP when any of these apply:

  1. Target is a packaged Electron app you cannot relaunch with --force-renderer-accessibility (Spotify, Steam, VS Code out of the box).
  2. Target uses Shadow DOM (open OR closed roots aside from cases below).
  3. UIA reports a Pane where DOM elements should be.
  4. is_visible() is unreliable because the app defers a11y-tree build-out.

If the app happily exposes elements to UIA, stay on UIA — it is faster and has no extra dependency.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# Install Dolphin with CDP support:
python -m pip install "dolphin-desktop[cdp]"

The [cdp] extra installs Playwright's client and driver. Connecting to an existing Electron, CEF or WebView2 debug endpoint uses that application's Chromium engine; a separate Playwright browser download is not required. Run python -m playwright install chromium only for a test or fixture that launches Playwright's own Chromium, such as the local examples/cdp/ demo. See PyPI installation before adding extras. Missing CDP dependencies produce an installation hint.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app, cdp = desktop.launch_electron_cdp(
    r'"C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe" --no-sandbox',
    debug_port=9222,
)

# Same 5 methods as the UIA Locator:
cdp.locator(".monaco-workbench").wait_for(state="visible")
cdp.locator("#status-bar").is_visible()
title = cdp.locator(".title").text()
cdp.locator("button.primary").click()
cdp.locator("input[name=username]").type_text("alice")

cdp.close()
app.kill()

launch_electron_cdp returns (Application, CDPSession):

  • Application is the same object as any other launched process — use app.kill(), app.detach(), app.window(...) for the native shell.
  • CDPSession is your DOM-side entry point.

The launcher verifies that the loopback CDP listener belongs to the launched process or its verified child process tree before handing it to Playwright. An HTTP 200 response from an unrelated process, a port collision, or an unverifiable listener owner fails closed and the launched process is cleaned up. Use a separate debug_port (and an application-specific isolated profile) for parallel sessions.

docs.title: Full API surface
docs.text:
CDPLocator mirrors dolphin_desktop.Locator so tests port between UIA and CDP without renaming methods:

Category Methods Mouse click(modifiers=, position=, button=, force=), double_click, right_click, hover, drag_to Keyboard focus, press_key, type_text, set_text, clear Form check, uncheck, select_option(value=/label=/index=), set_input_files Layout scroll_into_view, bounding_box State text, inner_html, value, get_attribute, is_visible, is_enabled, is_checked, exists, count Multi-match nth(i), first(), last(), all() Narrowing locator(sub), filter(has_text=/has=/has_not=/has_not_text=) A11y selectors get_by_role, get_by_label, get_by_text, get_by_placeholder, get_by_title, get_by_alt_text, get_by_test_id Wait wait_for(state=visible/hidden/attached/detached) Debug screenshot(path=None) — returns a PIL image Escape hatch element_handle() — raw Playwright handle for advanced use

CDPSession extras (page-level, not tied to a locator):

Method Purpose evaluate(js, *args) Run JavaScript in the page press_key(key) Global shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+P, Escape) screenshot(path=None) Full-page PIL image wait_for_load_state(state, timeout) Wait for load/domcontentloaded/networkidle wait_for_url(pattern, timeout) Wait until the URL matches current_url() Read the current URL reload(timeout) Reload the current page set_default_timeout(seconds) Change Playwright's default action timeout frame_locator(selector) Reach into an <iframe> accept_dialogs() / dismiss_dialogs() Auto-handle alert/confirm/prompt console_messages() / clear_console_messages() Capture / reset console log cookies() / set_cookies([...]) / clear_cookies() Read + write browser cookies local_storage_get/set/clear / session_storage_get/set/clear Storage helpers route(pattern, handler) / unroute(pattern) Network interception (mock API responses) expect_response(url_or_predicate, timeout) Context manager: capture a response expect_request(url_or_predicate, timeout) Context manager: capture a request expect_download(timeout) Context manager: catch the next file download expect_popup(timeout) Context manager: catch the next new window (auto-switches) add_init_script(js) Run JS on every page BEFORE its own scripts (mock Date.now, feature flags) get_by_role/label/text/placeholder/title/alt_text/test_id(...) A11y-first page-level selectors pages() / switch_to_page(i) Multi-window Electron close() / context-manager Detach cleanly

CDPRoute (yielded to route handlers) has respond(status, body, ...), respond_json(payload), pass_through(), abort(reason). CDPRequest (readonly view) exposes url, method, headers, resource_type, post_data, post_data_json. CDPDownload has suggested_filename, save_as(path), path(), cancel(), delete().

CDPFrameLocator (returned from session.frame_locator(sel)) chains locator(sub), get_by_role, get_by_text, get_by_label to reach into iframe DOM.

All exceptions surface as dolphin's ElementNotFoundError and WaitTimeoutError — user code catches the same types whether the backend is UIA or CDP.

docs.title: Attaching to an already-running app
docs.text:
If you started Electron manually (or a fixture is passing you a running PID) use CDPSession.connect(endpoint):

from dolphin_desktop import CDPSession

cdp = CDPSession.connect("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
cdp.locator("#login").click()
cdp.close()

docs.title: CEF apps (Steam, Spotify, some launchers)
docs.text:
CEF (Chromium Embedded Framework) speaks the same Chrome DevTools Protocol as Electron — once the debug port is up, CDPSession and CDPLocator work identically. Only the launch flag differs:

Runtime Flag Default port Electron --remote-debugging-port=9222 caller picks Steam -cef-enable-debugging (single dash) pinned to 8080 Other CEF usually --remote-debugging-port=N caller picks

Use Desktop.launch_cef_cdp:

from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

app, cdp = Desktop().launch_cef_cdp(
    r'"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steam.exe"',
    # debug_port=8080,                         # default — Steam hardcodes this
    # debug_flag="-cef-enable-debugging",      # default — Steam-specific
)

# Steam splits UI across many CEF pages (main, library, friends, overlay).
# Find the one you want by URL substring:
for i, p in enumerate(cdp.pages()):
    if "library" in p.url.lower():
        cdp.switch_to_page(i)
        break

owns_cs = "Counter-Strike" in cdp.evaluate("() => document.body.innerText")

Steam gotchas:

  • Launching a second steam.exe normally forwards to the running client without re-processing CLI args — so the debug flag is silently dropped. Kill the existing Steam first, or start Steam manually with -cef-enable-debugging and use CDPSession.connect("http://127.0.0.1:8080").
  • Steam signs you out when killed. The test fixture defaults to connect-only for this reason; opt in to auto-launch with DOLPHIN_STEAM_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1.
  • Library DOM is only rendered once the Library tab has been opened at least once. On a cold start document.body.innerText on the library page can be empty.

docs.title: Shadow DOM piercing
docs.text:
Playwright's CSS engine auto-pierces open shadow roots — descendant combinators work through the shadow boundary. For clarity and to match the explicit CDP contract, dolphin also supports the >> sub-locator combinator:

# both of these locate the same button inside an open shadow root
cdp.locator("#host #button-inside-shadow")
cdp.locator("#host >> #button-inside-shadow")

Closed shadow roots are not reachable via CDP — Chromium refuses to serialise them even to devtools. There is no workaround: the app owner has to expose an API or open the root. Document this at the boundary where your test starts, so downstream engineers know to fall back to image-based verification.

docs.title: Multi-window / multi-context Electron
docs.text:
Electron apps often open helper windows (settings, popouts). The CDPSession.pages() method returns every open page across every browser context:

pages = cdp.pages()
print([p.url for p in pages])
cdp.switch_to_page(1)          # subsequent locator() calls target that page

If the active page dies (window closed, hot-reload), session.page transparently picks the next durable page. This is what keeps module-scoped fixtures alive across many tests.

docs.title: Limitations vs. UIA
docs.text:
Concern UIA CDP Latency fast (in-process) ~5–20 ms per action (out-of-process WebSocket) Native menus / chrome full none (renderer only) Shadow DOM (open) usually invisible reachable Shadow DOM (closed) invisible invisible Requires app change no must start with --remote-debugging-port Extra dependency no playwright (~200 MB with Chromium install) Runs offline yes yes

Use both in the same test when you need to: UIA drives the native window frame (File → Open, menu bar, hover a system tray icon), CDP drives the DOM (form fills, click through a Shadow DOM component).

docs.title: Common failure modes
docs.text:
RuntimeError: Electron CDP debug port 9222 did not become live within 15s : The app never opened the port. Verify by manually running the same command and visiting http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version in a browser. Packaged Electron sometimes strips --remote-debugging-port — check the app's own docs.

TargetClosedError on every action after the first : You launched the app but pytest killed it between tests. Fix: call app.detach() after launch_electron_cdp in a module-scoped fixture so the plugin skips per-test PID reaping.

CDP connect_over_cdp('http://…') failed: connect ECONNREFUSED : Port is up but Chromium hasn't finished binding. Bump timeout= on the launch_electron_cdp call.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• examples/cdp/test_cdp.py — public CDP example using a local page.
  • docs/guides/electron.md — Electron via plain UIA when it does work.
  • docs/guides/image-based.md — last-resort fallback when nothing else sees the element.

docs.title: Image-Based Fallback
docs.text: Image matching is the fallback path for controls that UIA and Win32 cannot see. It uses OpenCV template matching and optional OCR through Tesseract.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install "dolphin-desktop[vision]"

OCR also requires the Tesseract executable to be installed separately.

docs.title: Capture A Template
docs.text:
dolphin spy --image-pick --output-dir templates

Use Ctrl+Click in the picker to save a PNG template.

docs.title: Use ImageLocator
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import ImageLocator

button = ImageLocator("templates/submit.png", threshold=0.9)
button.wait_for(timeout=10)
button.click()

Find without clicking:

point = button.find()
if point is not None:
    x, y = point

Find all matches:

for x, y in button.find_all():
    print(x, y)

docs.title: Scope To A Window
docs.text:
win.image("templates/submit.png", confidence=0.9).click()

window.image(...) restricts matching to the window bounding box when Dolphin can read it.

docs.title: Locator Fallback
docs.text:
Use a normal selector first and an image only as the last resort:

from dolphin_desktop import ImageLocator

win.locator(
    auto_id="btnSubmit",
    fallback=[{"title": "Submit", "control_type": "Button"}],
    image_fallback=ImageLocator("templates/submit.png", threshold=0.9),
).click()

The image fallback must point to a readable template. A missing template raises FileNotFoundError, and a corrupt or undecodable template raises ValueError, both with the image_fallback path in the diagnostic. When a valid template is not visible on the screen, normal locator resolution still reports ElementNotFoundError.

docs.title: OCR And Screen Helpers
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Screen

img = Screen.screenshot()
img.save("screen.png")

text = Screen.text()
point = Screen.find_text("Submitted")

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Keep templates small and specific.
  • Capture templates at the same DPI and theme used by CI.
  • Prefer UIA or Win32 selectors when available.
  • Use OCR for broad verification, not as the first choice for precise controls.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix ImportError: cv2 vision extra not installed pip install "dolphin-desktop[vision]" TesseractNotFoundError Tesseract exe not on PATH Install from https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/tesseract/wiki and add C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR to PATH Template matches wrong region Threshold too permissive Raise threshold towards 0.95 (default 0.85) and re-capture at exact DPI Match works locally, fails in CI DPI / theme / font-hinting difference Capture templates on the CI runner OS (use a screenshot from a failed CI run), commit both variants, and pick between them with platform.system() / your own CI env var Match works with English UI, fails in localised builds UI theme swapped icon Capture per-locale templates in templates/<locale>/ and pick the directory from your own locale setting OCR returns garbled Unicode Wrong language pack Screen.text() uses Tesseract's default language — install the language pack you need and set the TESSDATA_PREFIX / tesseract language configuration for the process Screen.find_image() extremely slow (>2 s) Full-screen template matching Constrain the search: Screen.find_image(template, region=(x1, y1, x2, y2)) Templates rot with UI updates Long-lived tests Inspect drift with dolphin selfheal-stats, then re-capture the templates it reports

docs.title: Java Swing / AWT
docs.text: Dolphin includes Java Access Bridge helpers for Swing and AWT applications on Windows.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A JRE or JDK with Java Access Bridge tools.
  • JAVA_HOME must be explicitly set to a trusted absolute JRE/JDK path containing bin\windowsaccessbridge-64.dll, even when Java Access Bridge is already enabled. Enabling it also requires bin\jabswitch.exe. Dolphin loads JAB exclusively from this JAVA_HOME\bin: registry discovery, System32, the working directory and PATH do not supply a fallback DLL.
  • A 64-bit Python interpreter is required to load this 64-bit bridge DLL.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch_java("java -jar MySwingApp.jar")
win = app.window(class_name="SunAwtFrame")

launch_java() calls JavaAccessBridge.ensure_enabled() before starting the process and initializes the JAB client session. ensure_enabled() first validates JAVA_HOME and the bridge DLL, even when Windows reports JAB as already enabled.

JavaAccessBridge.java_home() discovers a Java installation from JAVA_HOME or the registry without executing a search program or inspecting PATH. Discovery does not configure JAB. Use JavaAccessBridge.validate_configuration() to check the required explicit JAVA_HOME and DLL without loading or enabling the bridge; it returns the configured home or raises RuntimeError.

docs.title: Selectors
docs.text:
For Java windows, Window.get_by_* returns a JAB-backed locator.

win.get_by_role("text", name="Username").type_text("admin")
win.get_by_role("password text", name="Password").type_text("secret")
win.get_by_role("push button", name="Sign in").click()

Common role strings come from Java Access Bridge role_en_US, for example:

Swing control JAB role JButton push button JTextField text JPasswordField password text JCheckBox check box JRadioButton radio button JComboBox combo box JList list JTable table JTree tree

docs.title: Check Java Access Bridge
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import JavaAccessBridge

print(JavaAccessBridge.java_home())
print(JavaAccessBridge.is_enabled())
JavaAccessBridge.ensure_enabled()

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If jabswitch.exe or windowsaccessbridge-64.dll is missing, set JAVA_HOME to a trusted absolute JDK path that includes both files.
  • If the tree is empty immediately after launch, increase the app startup delay or wait for idle.
  • If roles differ from the table, inspect the app and use the exact role/name exposed by Java Access Bridge.

docs.title: Mainframe terminal (3270 / 5250) automation
docs.text:
dolphin_desktop drives IBM mainframe (3270, z/OS TSO/CICS) and midrange (5250, IBM i) sessions through three interchangeable backends:

Backend Command When to use s3270 (default) Spawns ws3270 / s3270 subprocess Open-source, 3270 hosts. CI-friendly. Requires wc3270 / x3270 package installed. tn5250 Pure-Python TN5250 client (no extra dependency) IBM i / AS400 hosts (pub400.com, banks, ERP). Real TN5250 negotiation, not NVT fallback. hllapi Attaches to a running enterprise emulator via EHLLAPI DLL Production: IBM PCOMM, Attachmate/Rocket Reflection, Micro Focus RUMBA.

All three backends implement the same MainframeTerminal surface — user code is portable between them.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop, AID, Secret

with Desktop().mainframe(host="tso.host.example", port=992, session_type="3270", tls=True) as term:
    term.wait_ready()
    term.field_after("USERID").type_text("MYUSER")
    term.field_after("PASSWORD").type_text(Secret("s3cret"))
    term.press(AID.ENTER)
    term.wait_change()
    assert term.screen().contains("READY")

Two habits worth adopting from the start:

  • tls=True — a terminal session carries the sign-on in the clear otherwise (see Transport security).
  • Secret(...) around a password — marks the value for Dolphin's diagnostic redaction while sending the actual value to the host.

docs.title: Migrating from the previous API
docs.text:
This release changes Desktop.mainframe() transport defaults and arguments. Replace tls_ca_file= with tls_cafile=. Use the certificate's DNS name as host; server_hostname= is no longer accepted. insecure_tls= is also removed: unverified TLS is unavailable, and an intentional remote plaintext session must use allow_plaintext=True. Existing remote plaintext calls need that explicit opt-in or tls=True. Port 992 does not enable TLS by itself.

A 3270/5250 session sends the user id and password in the same unencrypted byte stream as the rest of the screen; neither EBCDIC nor Telnet provides confidentiality. dolphin therefore refuses a plaintext connection to a remote host and asks you to choose:

# Verified TLS — certificate chain AND host name are checked. No fallback:
# a failed handshake raises, it never silently drops to plaintext.
term = desktop.mainframe(host="mf.example", port=992, session_type="3270", tls=True)

# Native TN5250 with an explicit trusted CA bundle.
term = desktop.mainframe(host="ibmi.example", port=992, session_type="5250",
                         backend="tn5250", tls=True,
                         tls_cafile=r"C:\ca\corp-root.pem")

# Native TN5250 with a caller-built context (must still verify the peer).
import ssl
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=r"C:\ca\corp-root.pem")
term = desktop.mainframe(host="ibmi.example", port=992, session_type="5250",
                         backend="tn5250", tls=True, tls_context=ctx)

# An SSH/stunnel tunnel terminated on localhost is exempt (loopback).
term = desktop.mainframe(host="127.0.0.1", port=3271, session_type="3270")

# Knowingly unencrypted (logged as a warning) — only through a channel
# you have secured by other means.
term = desktop.mainframe(host="mf.example", allow_plaintext=True)

The port number is never treated as a substitute for TLS — connecting to port 992 without tls=True is still refused. For the s3270 backend, tls=True opens the emulator's supported L: TLS tunnel (you may also write host="L:mf.example"); dolphin passes -verifycert explicitly and pins -accepthostname to the connected host after user arguments. It rejects switches and -xrm resources that disable verification or substitute another accepted hostname (-noverifycert, -noverifyhostcert, acceptHostname, verifyHostCert, selfSignedOk). The hllapi backend delegates the network side to the emulator, so configure TLS in the emulator's own session profile.

Unlike tn5250, where dolphin owns the TLS handshake and verifies it directly, s3270/ws3270 is an external process: dolphin can confirm the -cafile flag was accepted by the build, but the certificate verification itself happens inside the emulator, not in Python. dolphin explicitly passes -verifycert, but treats s3270 TLS as trustworthy as the installed emulator build, not as independently verified by dolphin — use backend="tn5250" when that independent verification matters.

docs.title: s3270 backend (open source, default)
docs.text:
On Windows, obtain wc3270 from the upstream x3270 project and locate its ws3270.exe. Pass its absolute path as ws3270_path= for a non-standard installation. The library also checks PATH and well-known wc3270 installation directories.

For a reproducible build, use the archive version and SHA-256 check pinned in the source checkout's .github/workflows/ci.yml. A public network host is not needed for the controlled protocol example in examples/mainframe/.

TLS trust follows the installed emulator build. In particular, Windows Schannel builds use the Windows certificate store; do not assume that passing a PEM CA file configures the same trust behavior as native Python TN5250 TLS. Configure the emulator's supported verified trust mechanism for the test host.

The native tn5250 backend needs no emulator executable. Its live-host write/submit limitation is described below.

docs.title: HLLAPI backend (enterprise emulators)
docs.text:
The emulator vendor ships an EHLAPI32.DLL (or PCSHLL32.DLL for IBM PCOMM). For security, dolphin_desktop does not search CWD, the application directory, or the ambient PATH for these names. Pass the vendor DLL through hllapi_dll_path as an existing absolute path. This argument is required for backend="hllapi"; no DLL is automatically discovered in Program Files or System32. Missing, relative or unusable paths raise MainframeError:

DLL name Vendor PCSHLL32.DLL IBM Personal Communications (PCOMM) EHLAPI32.DLL Attachmate / Rocket Reflection WHLAPI32.DLL Older Rocket versions

If the configured path cannot be loaded, the backend raises a clear error. The DLL must be a 32-bit or 64-bit build matching the Python interpreter (a 64-bit Python cannot load a 32-bit DLL). Check the configured vendor DLL's architecture rather than inferring it from the filename.

docs.title: MainframeTerminal
docs.text: Method Purpose connect(host, port, *, session_type, timeout) Open the session. Called automatically by Desktop.mainframe(connect=True). disconnect() Idempotent teardown. is_connected() Session-live probe. screen() -> TerminalScreen Fresh snapshot of the presentation space. text() -> str Convenience — screen().text(). field(row=, col=, length=) -> TerminalField Locator for a positional field. field_after(label, length=20, row=None) -> TerminalField Locator immediately after label — skips separator chars. type_text(text) Type at the current cursor position. press(aid) Send an AID key ("Enter", "PF3", "Clear" …). Use the AID class or raw strings. move_cursor(row, col) Move the input cursor. Only works in true 3270/5250 mode (see NVT note below). wait_ready(timeout) Block until the keyboard unlocks. wait_change(timeout) Block until the host writes to the screen. wait_for_text(needle, timeout, row=) Poll until needle appears. is_keyboard_locked() True while the host is still writing. context manager with desktop.mainframe(...) as term: auto-disconnects.

docs.title: s3270 input safety
docs.text: The s3270 backend sends one action per line to the emulator process. For that reason, host and type_text() values containing carriage returns, line feeds, NULs, or other control characters are rejected with MainframeError before the process is started or stdin is written. Host values containing s3270 action delimiters such as parentheses, semicolons, commas, equals signs, or spaces are rejected as well. Printable quotes and backslashes in text are escaped and remain a single literal String(...) action; text such as Quit() is not executed as an emulator command.

docs.title: TerminalScreen
docs.text:
Immutable 24×80 or 43×80 grid snapshot.

Property / method Purpose rows, cols Grid size. cursor -> (row, col) 1-indexed input cursor position. text() All rows joined by \n. line(row) Full text of one row. text_at(row, col, length) Substring — never IndexErrors past line end. contains(needle, row=None) Case-sensitive substring search. find(needle) -> (row, col) \| None First occurrence, 1-indexed.

docs.title: TerminalField
docs.text:
Bound to a specific (row, col, length).

Method Purpose read() Right-stripped current value. type_text(text, clear=True) Move cursor to field, clear it, type.

docs.title: AID
docs.text: Attribute AID key AID.ENTER Enter AID.CLEAR Clear AID.PA1 / PA2 / PA3 Program Attention keys — 3270 only. The s3270 and hllapi backends send them; the native tn5250 backend raises, because 5250 has no equivalent key to substitute. AID.pf(n) "PF1" .. "PF24"

docs.title: Choosing a live IBM i host
docs.text:
An IBM i host uses TN5250. A successful NVT banner through a TN3270 emulator is not evidence of 5250 support. Select backend="tn5250" for the native read/negotiation path, or an appropriate HLLAPI emulator for write-critical flows. Configure the host, port and verified TLS trust for your environment.

For a reproducible local protocol example without an external IBM system, use examples/mainframe/test_mainframe.py in the source checkout.

docs.title: Native TN5250 backend status
docs.text:
The pure-Python TN5250 backend (backend="tn5250") implements Telnet negotiation (BINARY, EOR, TERMINAL-TYPE and NEW-ENVIRON), WriteToDisplay parsing for SBA/IC/RA/SF orders and inline display attributes, field detection and screen/cursor reads. It does not use NVT as a 5250 fallback.

Known limitations:

  • The write/submit path is unverified against live IBM i hosts. Unit checks of generated input records do not establish that a host processes Enter/PF keys or updates the intended fields. Use HLLAPI with a prepared enterprise emulator for write-critical 5250 flows and validate that setup.
  • Write Structured Field (WSF) support is absent. Hosts requiring those commands need a different backend or additional implementation.

The s3270 backend supports 3270 only. session_type="5250" is rejected; select tn5250 or HLLAPI for IBM i rather than relying on raw Telnet/NVT.

Controlled local round trips are available in tests/mainframe/mock_tn3270/ and are also used by examples/mainframe/test_mainframe.py. A local protocol run does not establish compatibility with a particular external IBM host or emulator configuration.

docs.title: Backend selection
docs.text:
# Default — s3270 subprocess (3270 hosts)
term = desktop.mainframe(host="host.example", tls=True, session_type="3270")

# Explicit s3270 with custom binary path
term = desktop.mainframe(
    host="host.example", tls=True,
    ws3270_path=r"D:\tools\wc3270\ws3270.exe",
    model="3279-2",           # 24x80 instead of 43x80
)

# Native TN5250 — for IBM i / AS400 hosts (pub400, banks, ERP AS400)
term = desktop.mainframe(
    host="ibmi.example",
    port=992,
    session_type="5250",
    backend="tn5250",
    tls=True,
)
# Pure-Python client, zero external dependency. Negotiates real 5250
# (not NVT fallback like s3270). Parses WriteToDisplay commands into
# a 24×80 EBCDIC screen buffer with field detection.

# HLLAPI — attach to a running PCOMM session "A"
term = desktop.mainframe(
    backend="hllapi",
    session_id="A",
    hllapi_dll_path=r"C:\Program Files\IBM\Personal Communications\PCSHLL32.DLL",
)

The host, port, and session_type arguments are recorded on the MainframeTerminal but ignored by the HLLAPI backend — the emulator manages the network side there.

docs.title: Common failure modes
docs.text:
No ws3270/s3270 binary found : Install wc3270 on Windows — see the install section. Pass ws3270_path= for non-standard installs.

No HLLAPI-compatible DLL found : The emulator either is not installed or exposes a differently-named DLL. Pass hllapi_dll_path= with the absolute path. Check the DLL's bitness matches the Python interpreter.

the s3270 backend speaks TN3270 only ... : session_type="5250" on the default s3270 backend raises a MainframeError — x3270 has no 5250 support. Use backend="tn5250" for IBM i / AS/400 hosts, or session_type="3270" if the host really is a 3270 host.

MoveCursor() is not valid in NVT mode : The host did not accept TN3270/TN3270E negotiation — connection fell back to plain telnet. move_cursor() and positional AID keys are unavailable; only sequential typing works. Check the host's protocol; a 5250-only IBM i host requires tn5250 or HLLAPI.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• tests/mainframe/mock_tn3270/ — controlled local protocol regressions.
  • x3270 project — upstream emulator suite.
  • EHLLAPI reference (IBM) — HLLAPI function-code table.

docs.title: Native Windows Apps
docs.text: Use this guide for Win32, WPF, WinForms, MFC, Delphi/VCL, and similar Windows desktop applications.

docs.title: Choose A Backend
docs.text:
App type Start with Notes WPF uia Prefer AutomationId selectors when developers set them WinForms uia Use win32 for older controls that expose poor UIA data Modern Win32 uia Inspect with dolphin spy before choosing selectors MFC, Delphi/VCL, VB6 win32 Class names are often more useful than UIA roles 
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop(backend="uia")

For legacy applications:

desktop = Desktop.for_legacy_apps()

docs.title: WPF / WinForms Example
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch("MyApp.exe")
win = app.window(title_re=".*My Application.*")

win.get_by_automation_id("txtUsername").type_text("admin")
win.get_by_automation_id("txtPassword").type_text("secret")
win.get_by_automation_id("btnSignIn").click()

assert win.get_by_automation_id("lblStatus").text() == "Signed in"

docs.title: Legacy Win32 Example
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop

desktop = Desktop(backend="win32")
app = desktop.launch("LegacyApp.exe")
win = app.window(title="Main Window")

win.get_by_class("Edit").type_text("hello")
win.get_by_class("Button").click()

docs.title: Convenience controls on the win32 backend
docs.text:
The typed shortcuts locate their controls on win32 too, for classic HWND controls (MFC, VB6, Delphi/VCL) and WinForms alike:

win = Desktop.for_legacy_apps().launch("LegacyApp.exe").window(title="Main Window")

win.edit().set_text("Dolphin")
win.combo_box().select_item("Premium")
win.tree().select_item_by_path("Root", "Child")
win.list_box().items()                    # ["Alpha", "Beta", ...]
win.tab().select_tab("Advanced")
win.check_box(name="Remember").exists()   # a BS_CHECKBOX, not the "Save" button
win.menu("File").item("Show dialog").click()
win.locator(title="ready", control_type="Static").wait_for()

The win32 backend has no UI Automation control types. A UIA-style control_type (Edit, ComboBox, Tree, List, Button, CheckBox, RadioButton, Group, Text, Tab, ToolBar, StatusBar, ProgressBar, Slider, Spinner, Header, Calendar) is matched against pywinauto's friendly class name for the window instead. That name covers the classic, WinForms (WindowsForms10.EDIT.*), VB6 and VCL class spellings, and tells check boxes, radio buttons and group boxes apart from push buttons by their BS_* style. The win32 friendly names themselves (Static, TreeView, ListBox, ListView, TabControl, …) are accepted as control_type too, and a dotted .NET type such as "System.Windows.Forms.TextBox" keeps pywinauto's own WinForms meaning.

  • tree() drives SysTreeView32 nodes through tree-view messages: select_item_by_path selects the node, and the application gets the same selection-changed notification a click produces.
  • menu() / .item() resolve a native menu bar (HMENU) by exact item text, ignoring & mnemonics and \t shortcuts. click() clicks the item with the mouse; invoke() sends its WM_COMMAND without any input. A WinForms MenuStrip/ToolStrip is a control, not an HMENU; locate it with the uia backend instead. && in a caption is a literal ampersand, so R&&D is named R&D. exists() and is_enabled() read the menu whether or not it is open. is_visible(), wait_for() and wait_until_hidden() mean on screen, and unlike on uia they never open the parent menu. is_checked() reads a checkable item the same way, and check() / uncheck() send its WM_COMMAND only when the state differs. An application that sets check marks when the popup opens, as MFC ON_UPDATE_COMMAND_UI handlers do, reports the state from the last time the popup was open.
  • A UIA type with no Win32 window class of its own (MenuItem outside a menu chain, TreeItem, ListItem, Hyperlink, Pane, Window, …) raises UnsupportedCapabilityError at once, from wait_for() and exists() alike, instead of timing out. Select such elements by class_name / title, or use the uia backend.
  • all() and count() apply every criterion, including control_id, title_re and class_name_re, as does the count behind a negative nth(). all() and count() include hidden controls and every nested level. A negative nth() counts what its lookup can select: visible controls for actions, hidden ones too for exists().
  • list_box() reads items() and selected_items() from a LISTBOX or a SysListView32 (first column of each row) through their own messages, and select_item() selects an entry.
  • tab().select_tab(name) selects a SysTabControl32 tab by exact text, ignoring an & mnemonic, including with the TCS_BUTTONS style, and the application switches pages as on a click. If the selection does not change, for example because the application refuses it, it raises WaitTimeoutError.
  • text() on an empty plain edit box or label returns "" straight away. Only a RichEdit or other control whose text the window text does not carry falls back to select-all and the clipboard.

docs.title: Inspect The UI Tree
docs.text:
dolphin spy --window "My Application" --depth 3
dolphin spy --pick

Prefer stable selectors:

  1. get_by_automation_id(...)
  2. get_by_role(..., name=...)
  3. get_by_title(...)
  4. get_by_class(...)

docs.title: Common Dialogs
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import FileDialog, MessageBox

win.get_by_title("Open").click()
dlg = FileDialog.wait_for(timeout=10)
dlg.set_path(r"C:\Temp\input.txt")
dlg.confirm()

win.get_by_title("Delete").click()
msg = MessageBox.wait_for(timeout=10)
msg.click_yes()

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Avoid title-only selectors for localized applications.
  • If the application runs as Administrator, run the test process as Administrator too.
  • If UIA shows little useful information, try --dolphin-backend=win32 or Desktop.for_legacy_apps().

docs.title: Office
docs.text: Dolphin automates Excel, Word, PowerPoint and classic Outlook through COM wrappers. These helpers require the corresponding Microsoft Office applications and pywin32 on Windows.

docs.title: Supported applications
docs.text: The dedicated Office COM API exports ExcelApp, WordApp, PowerPointApp and OutlookApp from dolphin_desktop. Outlook requires classic Outlook with an existing configured MAPI profile; new Outlook is outside this COM API. Ribbon controls and dialogs still use the generic Desktop UIA/Win32 API. See the Support Matrix.

docs.title: Macro security
docs.text:
ExcelApp.open() and WordApp.open() default to allow_macros=False. They set AutomationSecurity=3 immediately before opening the file to disable VBA macros, then restore the previous value in finally, including when opening fails. Excel also sets AskToUpdateLinks=False and opens with UpdateLinks=0; Word sets Options.UpdateLinksAtOpen=False to prevent automatic OLE link updates and restores its previous value in finally. Enabling macros does not enable these external link updates. See Microsoft's UpdateLinksAtOpen documentation.

Macro execution requires explicit trust

allow_macros=True selects msoAutomationSecurityLow (1). VBA macros can execute arbitrary code with your account's permissions. Use this opt-in only with trusted documents. Office policies, Protected View and other security controls can still prevent execution; Dolphin does not bypass them.

from dolphin_desktop import ExcelApp, WordApp

# Explicitly permit macros only in files whose code you trust.
with ExcelApp.open("trusted.xlsm", allow_macros=True) as xl:
    print(xl.active_sheet.name)

with WordApp.open("trusted.docm", allow_macros=True) as wd:
    print(wd.active_document.name)

AutomationSecurity=3 does not disable Excel 4.0/XLM macros; Excel can still display a security prompt for them. Enforce XLM restrictions through Office policy and never approve active content from an untrusted file. See Microsoft's AutomationSecurity documentation. UpdateLinks=0 controls workbook external links, not every data connection or other type of active content. These wrappers are not a document sandbox.

The security setting applies to the file opened by open() and is restored afterwards. connect() does not change security or disable macros in documents already open. Documents remain editable because the API supports modifying and saving them; read-only mode would not itself prevent macro execution.

docs.title: Security regression checks
docs.text:
Run the deterministic COM stand-in tests without Office or real macros:

uv run pytest tests/framework/test_office_com.py tests/framework/test_office.py -q

The synthetic auto-open macro only increments an in-memory counter. Tests cover default blocking, explicit opt-in, link arguments, restoration after errors, rejected security settings, a simulated policy block and an XLM prompt. These checks verify the wrapper contract, not the Office macro engine.

docs.title: Real Office acceptance
docs.text: Real Office validation requires reviewed macro fixtures, safety/cleanup checks and isolated Office installations. Preserve organization policies. A blocked positive control is incomplete verification of the macro engine. Record Office versions, policies, passing cases and skips with each run.

docs.title: Excel
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import ExcelApp

with ExcelApp.open("report.xlsx") as xl:
    wb = xl.active_workbook
    sheet = wb.sheet("Sheet1")

    sheet.cell(1, 1).value = "Name"
    sheet.cell(1, 2).value = "Score"
    sheet.cell(2, 1).value = "Alice"
    sheet.cell(2, 2).value = 95

    wb.save()

Read a range:

with ExcelApp.open("report.xlsx") as xl:
    rows = xl.active_workbook.sheet("Sheet1").range("A1:B2").as_list()

Connect to an already running Excel instance:

with ExcelApp.connect() as xl:
    print(xl.active_sheet.name)

open() and connect() own different things

open() starts a private Excel instance, so leaving the with block closes the workbooks it opened and quits that instance. connect() attaches to the operator's running Excel — leaving the block closes nothing and quits nothing, because those workbooks are not yours. The same rule applies to WordApp.

docs.title: Word
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import WordApp

with WordApp.open("template.docx") as wd:
    doc = wd.active_document
    doc.find_replace("{{NAME}}", "Alice")
    doc.save_as("output.docx")

Connect to an already running Word instance:

with WordApp.connect() as wd:
    print(wd.active_document.name)

A connected instance is left running when the block exits — see the note above.

docs.title: PowerPoint
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import PowerPointApp

with PowerPointApp.create(visible=False) as ppt:
    presentation = ppt.active_presentation
    slide = presentation.add_slide()  # blank layout, appended at the end
    caption = slide.add_textbox("Quarterly report")
    caption.text = "Quarterly report — reviewed"
    presentation.save_as("report.pptx")
    presentation.export_pdf("report.pdf")

with PowerPointApp.open("report.pptx", visible=False) as ppt:
    print(ppt.active_presentation.slide(1).shape(1).text)

Slide and shape indexes are 1-based; shapes can also be selected by name.

Text formatting is exposed on shapes and on character ranges, so a test can assert how a slide looks, not only what it says:

title = slide.add_textbox("Revenue up 12%", left=50, top=40, width=500, height=60)
title.bold = True
title.font_size = 32
title.font_color = (200, 0, 0)
title.characters(12, 3).italic = True  # "12%" only, 1-based positions

assert title.bold is True
assert title.italic is None            # mixed: part of the box is italic
assert title.characters(12, 3).italic is True
assert slide.shape_names == [title.name]

logo = slide.add_picture("logo.png", left=600, top=40)
assert not logo.has_text and logo.width > 0
presentation.move_slide(presentation.slide_count, 1)  # bring the last slide first

Formatting reads return None when a range mixes values. Pictures are embedded, never linked, so the saved file does not depend on the source path.

Tables, charts, speaker notes, layout titles and hyperlinks are covered too:

slide = presentation.add_slide(layout=11)          # title-only layout
slide.title = "Q3 by region"
slide.notes = "Mention the EMEA restatement."

table = slide.add_table(3, 2, values=[["Region", "Revenue"], ["EMEA", 120], ["APAC", 95]])
assert table.table.values[1] == ["EMEA", "120"]
table.table.cell(1, 1).bold = True

chart = slide.add_chart(["Q1", "Q2", "Q3"], {"EMEA": [100, 110, 120]}, title="EMEA trend")
assert chart.chart.series_values("EMEA") == [100.0, 110.0, 120.0]

link = slide.add_textbox("Full report")
link.hyperlink = "https://example.test/report"   # clickable in a slide show
link.hyperlink = ""                              # removes the link again

Setting hyperlink writes the address and sets the mouse-click action to ppActionHyperlink, so the link works in a slide show, not only in the editor. An empty string turns the action off and deletes the hyperlink; a blank address such as " " raises ValueError.

add_chart() writes each series as literal arrays on the chart, so the embedded Excel workbook is never opened and Excel does not need to be installed. PowerPoint only inserts charts into a presentation that has a document window, so build chart decks with create(visible=True) / open(visible=True); on a hidden presentation add_chart() raises RuntimeError instead of a bare COM error. Reading an existing chart works on hidden presentations too. A visible shared PowerPoint stays open after quit(); pass exclusive=True when the test should also end the process. To check the exported PDF itself (page count, text), parse it with a PDF library in your test. The repository's own live tests do that with pypdf. open() disables VBA macros by default and restores the previous AutomationSecurity setting after opening, including on failure. As with the other Office wrappers, allow_macros=True is an explicit opt-in for trusted files; Office policies still apply. This is not a sandbox for linked content. Opening a presentation already open in PowerPoint raises RuntimeError so the wrapper cannot accidentally take ownership of the operator's document.

PowerPoint is a shared COM server. connect() attaches to its active presentation; open() / create() expose the presentation they opened/created even when it has no window. In shared mode, quit() and context exit close only those owned presentations and release COM references, preserving the process. Save explicitly or use quit(save_changes=True) to retain changes. Failed saves/closes raise and keep the affected presentation available for retry.

export_pdf() uses PowerPoint's ExportAsFixedFormat with PDF output. Real acceptance tests must parse the resulting PDF and verify page count/content, not just check COM arguments or the file extension.

docs.title: Classic Outlook
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import OutlookApp, OutlookMail

with OutlookApp.start() as outlook:  # starts or reuses classic Outlook
    draft = outlook.create_mail(subject="Local report", body="Review the attachment.")
    draft.add_attachment("report.pdf")
    draft.save_as("report.msg")  # local file only; does not send

with OutlookApp.start() as outlook:
    mail = outlook.open_item("report.msg")
    assert isinstance(mail, OutlookMail)
    print(mail.subject, mail.body)
    mail.attachment(1).save_as("report-copy.pdf")
    print(outlook.default_folder("inbox").item_count)

connect() requires an already running classic Outlook session. start() may reuse the operator's session; neither method logs on/off or configures profiles. start() checks registered MAPI profiles before COM activation, then validates the active profile and accessible stores. Missing/unusable profiles raise RuntimeError. Missing folders/items raise LookupError. Folders support item(1) and folder("Child"); supported default folder names are inbox, drafts, sent, deleted, calendar, or an OlDefaultFolders integer. Items other than mail and appointments raise TypeError on lookup.

Drafts created by this OutlookApp support move(folder) and delete(). move() updates the existing wrapper to the COM object returned by Outlook; find_item(entry_id) can verify its absence/presence in source/destination folders. Folder lookup recognizes owned drafts by EntryID and StoreID. Pre-existing messages, sent messages and locally opened MSG files cannot be moved/deleted by this API. Destinations must come from the creating facade.

delete() moves an owned draft to its store's Deleted Items folder. A repeated call raises instead of silently deleting permanently. For UAT data cleanup, delete(permanent=True) explicitly removes only an owned draft already there.

create_appointment(subject=...) returns a calendar item with editable start and end Python datetimes (Outlook local time), location, subject and body. It can be saved to a local MSG file or explicitly persisted to the calendar with save(). Creating/saving appointments does not send invitations.

Mail supports to, cc, bcc, subject, body, html_body and attachments. save() stores a draft; only an explicit mail.send() sends a message using Outlook's configured account. Outlook security prompts/policies remain active. Context exit and quit() discard unsaved changes to only the items created or opened here; saved drafts/appointments remain saved. Items retrieved from existing folders are not automatically closed. Shared Outlook sessions are preserved. Failed saves/closes raise and retain the affected items for retry.

docs.title: A disposable profile for automation
docs.text:
OutlookApp.start() requires a configured MAPI profile. Use a dedicated profile with one local PST and no mail account for tests that create, move or delete items. Verify store and folder ownership before any mutation, and explicitly opt in to destructive operations in your test configuration.

Permanent deletion goes through a proxy re-fetched by EntryID: on PST stores Outlook silently ignores Delete() on the proxy that Move() returned, so the facade re-fetches after every move and verifies the outcome. The verification re-fetches the item: an unambiguous MAPI_E_NOT_FOUND confirms it is gone, and any other failure (a store, session or permission error) is treated as an unknown outcome and raised as RuntimeError, never reported as a successful delete.

docs.title: Exclusive Office sessions for UAT
docs.text:
PowerPointApp.create/open(..., exclusive=True) and OutlookApp.start(exclusive=True) require no existing process of that Office application. Use a dedicated test account without concurrent Office launches. This mode verifies the new process's image/creation time and retains its process handle. owns_process and process_id expose the resulting ownership.

After COM activation, exclusive startup polls process visibility for up to five seconds, servicing COM messages between attempts. Multiple candidates or a failed identity check stop initialization immediately. Failed activation, visibility timeout or ownership verification reports observed PIDs and a final snapshot of possible orphaned processes. A failed snapshot is reported as unknown, not as absence. No unverified process is claimed or terminated; inspect the reported processes before retrying. Office may still start after the timeout, so a diagnostic snapshot without candidates cannot prove that no process will appear later.

After document/item cleanup, quit() calls Application.Quit(), releases COM references and waits for that process handle to signal exit while pumping COM messages. A shutdown timeout raises and can be retried; processes are never force-killed. Foreign open presentations block exclusive PowerPoint shutdown. Objects from a closed facade are no longer usable. Shared mode (the default) and connect() never acquire process ownership or quit the operator's session.

For end-to-end validation, distinguish pre-existing and owned processes and check exported PDF content independently. Use a configured nonproduction Outlook profile and controlled draft folders. Create only synthetic drafts, verify move/delete outcomes and clean up saved items even after failures. To check missing-profile handling, use a Windows account without configured profiles and verify that no Outlook process starts.

Repeat on Office 2019 and Microsoft 365, x86 and x64, recording product/version/ bitness per run. A successful run on one installation does not establish PASS for another, and skipped profile-dependent scenarios do not count as PASS.

docs.title: Combining UI And Office Checks
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop, ExcelApp, FileDialog

desktop = Desktop()
app = desktop.launch("MyDataApp.exe")
win = app.window(title="Data Export")
win.get_by_title("Export").click()

dlg = FileDialog.wait_for(timeout=10)
dlg.set_path(r"C:\Temp\export.xlsx")
dlg.confirm()

with ExcelApp.open(r"C:\Temp\export.xlsx") as xl:
    sheet = xl.active_workbook.sheet("Sheet1")
    assert sheet.cell(1, 1).text == "Name"

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Context managers call quit() on exit.
  • ExcelApp.connect() and WordApp.connect() attach to the active Office instance.
  • COM automation is process-global and should not be used casually from parallel tests.

docs.title: Oracle Forms automation
docs.text: dolphin_desktop automates Oracle Forms Java clients — the Java Web Start applet, Forms Standalone Launcher (FSAL), or a plain Java main class — through the Java Access Bridge (JAB). The public surface speaks Forms concepts (blocks, items, function keys, LOV, status line) rather than raw Swing components, so tests port cleanly across Forms 10g / 11g / 12c and remain readable.

docs.title: What works
docs.text:
• JAB reads and writes. Item type_text(clear=True) first tries setTextContents; reads use the target's accessible text/value interfaces. Buttons and menu items first try accessible actions. These paths can avoid physical input, but missing actions or editable-text support can trigger a foreground mouse/keyboard fallback. clear=False also uses keyboard input. Verify the selected operations before relying on background execution.
  • Function keys. Unmodified keys use window-targeted messages. Shift/Ctrl/Alt combinations require foreground input; see the key-binding and modifier limitations below.
  • Menu bar navigation via ALT+first-letter mnemonic and JAB action invocation on the resolved menu item.
  • List of Values (F9) wrapper — .lov().select("SMITH") opens and completes the LOV popup.
  • Status line reader — pulls the current text from AccessibleContext.getAccessibleDescription() (the standard place Oracle Forms publishes dynamic status text).

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop import Desktop, OracleFormsKey

app = Desktop().launch_oracle_forms(
    jnlp="https://forms.example.com/forms/frmservlet?config=hr",
)
form = app.form()
form.wait_ready(timeout=30)

# Type into a block item, run the query, save.
app.block("EMPLOYEES").item("EMPNO").type_text("7369")
app.execute_query()             # F8
assert "Record 1" in app.status_line()
app.save()                      # F10 (see caveat below)

# LOV
app.list_of_values()            # F9
app.lov().select("JONES")

# Menu bar
app.menu("Query").select("Enter")

docs.title: Function-key reference
docs.text:
This table is an all-or-nothing choice

The Forms runtime loads exactly one key-binding resource file and every key comes from it. The values below follow the PC-style family (fmrpcweb.res). A host running the stock fmrweb.res uses a different family — and there, these bindings mean:

  • duplicate_record() → Exit, discarding uncommitted changes
  • insert_record() → Clear Record
  • delete_record() → Duplicate Record
  • clear_form() → Next Primary Key

Press Ctrl+K ("Show Keys") in the running form to see what your runtime actually loaded. If it does not match, override the whole block — never a single entry, because a borrowed entry silently maps to a different Forms function.

Attribute Key Oracle Forms action HELP F1 Help topic COUNT_QUERY Shift+F2 Count matching records ¹ DUPLICATE_ITEM F3 Copy item from previous record ¹ DUPLICATE_RECORD F4 Copy the previous record CLEAR_RECORD Shift+F4 Clear current record CLEAR_BLOCK Shift+F5 Clear all records in block ¹ INSERT_RECORD F6 Insert new record DELETE_RECORD Shift+F6 Delete current record ENTER_QUERY F7 Enter query mode CLEAR_FORM Shift+F7 Clear all records in form ¹ EXECUTE_QUERY F8 Run the query LIST_OF_VALUES F9 Open LOV popup SAVE / COMMIT F10 Save changes NEXT_ITEM Tab Move to next item PREVIOUS_ITEM Shift+Tab Move to previous item NEXT_RECORD Shift+Down Move to next record PREVIOUS_RECORD Shift+Up Move to previous record NEXT_BLOCK Shift+Page_Down Move to next block ¹ PREVIOUS_BLOCK Shift+Page_Up Move to previous block ¹ CLEAR_ITEM Ctrl+U Clear current item EXIT / CANCEL_QUERY Ctrl+Q Exit form / leave query mode

¹ Consistent with the PC-style family but not confirmed against a published resource file — verify with Ctrl+K before relying on it.

There is no First Record or Last Record function in the Forms key table, so the library exposes no binding for them. On a stock-file host F11 is Enter Query, which is why a "go to first record" helper built on F11 would silently put the block into query mode.

Modifier shortcuts need the foreground. PostMessage cannot set the target thread's modifier state, so anything with Shift+/Ctrl+ is delivered by SendInput against the foreground window. Unmodified keys (F7, F8, F9, F10) work from background runs, RDP sessions and CI hosts; modifier combos need a usable input desktop.

Send any of these with app.function_key(OracleFormsKey.X) or use the named shortcuts (app.enter_query(), app.execute_query(), …).

F10 caveat. Swing intercepts F10 for menu-bar activation before the InputMap fires. In real Forms 12c the Save keybinding still works because Forms overrides the default; a Swing host can instead open the menu bar. If your target Forms build has the same limitation, use app.menu("Action").select("Save") instead.

docs.title: Enabling the Java Access Bridge
docs.text:
The JAB is bundled with Adoptium and Oracle JDKs. dolphin's JavaAccessBridge handles the setup automatically, or run once by hand:

jabswitch.exe /enable

The JVM the Forms client uses must be launched with -Djava.accessibility=true (dolphin's launch_oracle_forms adds this flag by default) so the JVM loads the JAB helper on startup.

The bridge DLL and jabswitch.exe are loaded/run only from the absolute JAVA_HOME\bin location configured explicitly in the environment. Dolphin does not load a bare windowsaccessbridge-64.dll or jabswitch.exe name from the current directory or ambient PATH; keep JAVA_HOME pointed at a trusted JRE/JDK installation. If that absolute JDK path or executable is unavailable, initialization fails closed.

docs.title: Backend selection
docs.text:
# Java Web Start (real Oracle Forms deployment)
app = desktop.launch_oracle_forms(jnlp="https://forms.example.com/frmservlet")

# Forms Standalone Launcher (FSAL) — bundled JAR
app = desktop.launch_oracle_forms(jar=r"C:\forms\frmsal.jar")

# Local Java main class (used by the integration test suite)
app = desktop.launch_oracle_forms(
    main_class="OracleFormsMock",
    classpath=r"C:\path\to\classes",
)

# Attach to an already-running client — no launch
app = desktop.attach_oracle_forms(title_re=".*HR Payroll Form.*")

docs.title: Item locator convention
docs.text:
Oracle Forms items are named BLOCK.ITEM in the accessible tree (.getAccessibleContext().setAccessibleName("EMPLOYEES.EMPNO")). .block("EMPLOYEES").item("EMPNO") tries the qualified name first, then falls back to the plain item name.
