class PowerPointTable(_ComOwner):
    """A table shape's grid; rows and columns are 1-based like PowerPoint."""

    @property
    def rows(self) -> int:
        return int(self._com.Rows.Count)

    @property
    def columns(self) -> int:
        return int(self._com.Columns.Count)

    def cell(self, row: int, column: int) -> PowerPointTextRange:
        """The text of one cell as a formattable range."""
        return self._adopt(
            PowerPointTextRange(self._com.Cell(row, column).Shape.TextFrame.TextRange)
        )

    def row_values(self, row: int) -> list[str]:
        return [self.cell(row, column).text for column in range(1, self.columns + 1)]

    @property
    def values(self) -> list[list[str]]:
        """All cell texts, row by row."""
        return [self.row_values(row) for row in range(1, self.rows + 1)]

    def set_values(self, rows: Sequence[Sequence[Any]], *, start_row: int = 1) -> None:
        """Write *rows* into the table from *start_row*; the grid must be large enough.

        Every row is validated before the first cell is written, so data that
        does not fit leaves the table unchanged rather than partially updated.
        """
        values = _validate_table_fit(
            rows, total_rows=self.rows, total_columns=self.columns, start_row=start_row
        )
        for offset, row_values in enumerate(values):
            row = start_row + offset
            for column, value in enumerate(row_values, start=1):
                self.cell(row, column).text = str(value)

    def add_row(self, before: int | None = None) -> None:
        """Append a row, or insert one before the 1-based *before* row."""
        if before is None:
            self._com.Rows.Add()
        else:
            self._com.Rows.Add(before)

    def add_column(self, before: int | None = None) -> None:
        if before is None:
            self._com.Columns.Add()
        else:
            self._com.Columns.Add(before)

    def delete_row(self, row: int) -> None:
        self._com.Rows(row).Delete()

    def delete_column(self, column: int) -> None:
        self._com.Columns(column).Delete()

class OutlookApp:
    """COM API for classic Outlook with an existing configured MAPI profile.

    No implicit sending, logon or logoff occurs. Context exit closes owned items.
    Shared sessions are preserved; exclusive sessions also quit their own process.
    New Outlook does not provide this COM object model.
    """

    def __init__(self, _com: Any, *, _session: _OfficeSession | None = None) -> None:
        self._com = _com
        self._session = _session
        self._opened: list[OutlookItem] = []
        self._namespace: Any = None
        self._resources: list[Any] = []

    @property
    def owns_process(self) -> bool:
        """Whether this exclusive session still owns a process awaiting confirmed exit."""
        return self._session is not None and not self._session.closed

    @property
    def process_id(self) -> int | None:
        """Verified exclusive process ID, or None for shared/connected sessions."""
        return self._session.pid if self._session is not None else None

    def _validate_profile(self) -> None:
        try:
            namespace = self._com.GetNamespace("MAPI")
            if not namespace.CurrentProfileName or namespace.Stores.Count < 1:
                raise ValueError("No active profile or accessible store")
            self._namespace = namespace
        except Exception as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("Outlook MAPI profile unavailable or no accessible store") from exc

    def _fresh_item(self, com: Any) -> Any:
        """Re-fetch *com* by its (EntryID, StoreID) after a Move().

        The proxy Move() returns on a PST store is only half alive: Delete() on
        it silently does nothing, so later operations must act on a handle
        Outlook fully honours. Re-fetching can be genuinely unsupported by a
        store/provider (MAPI_E_NO_SUPPORT / E_NOTIMPL); only then is the original
        handle the best available and kept as a deliberate fallback. Any other
        failure -- access, session, store, a different COM code, or a non-COM
        error -- leaves the outcome uncertain and must not be masked by handing
        back a proxy that may silently drop a later Delete(): it raises
        RuntimeError instead.
        """
        try:
            entry_id, store_id = str(com.EntryID), str(com.Parent.StoreID)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Could not read the moved Outlook item's identity to re-fetch it; "
                f"its state is uncertain ({exc})"
            ) from exc
        try:
            return self._namespace.GetItemFromID(entry_id, store_id)
        except Exception as exc:
            if _com_status_code(exc) in _REFETCH_UNSUPPORTED:
                return com
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Could not re-fetch the moved Outlook item; its state is uncertain ({exc})"
            ) from exc

    def _refetch_or_same(self, com: Any) -> Any:
        """Best-effort re-fetch by (EntryID, StoreID); return *com* on any failure.

        Used only where a later explicit check -- not this re-fetch -- is the
        authority on the outcome: permanent delete re-fetches merely to act on a
        fully-honoured proxy and then proves removal with _item_still_present, so
        a re-fetch failure here is not itself a reason to fail (unlike move(),
        whose result is kept and used later; see _fresh_item).
        """
        try:
            return self._namespace.GetItemFromID(str(com.EntryID), str(com.Parent.StoreID))
        except Exception:
            return com

    def _item_still_present(self, entry_id: str, store_id: str) -> bool:
        """Whether the item is still retrievable; raise when the result is uncertain.

        A permanent delete is confirmed gone only by an unambiguous
        MAPI_E_NOT_FOUND from Outlook. Any other failure to resolve the item
        (a store, session or permission error, a different COM code, or a
        non-COM exception) leaves the outcome unknown and raises, so a
        permanent delete is never reported as done on a guess.
        """
        try:
            self._namespace.GetItemFromID(entry_id, store_id)
            return True
        except Exception as lookup_error:
            if _com_status_code(lookup_error) == _MAPI_E_NOT_FOUND:
                return False
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Could not verify permanent deletion: Outlook did not report the item "
                f"as not-found, so the outcome is unknown ({lookup_error})"
            ) from lookup_error

    def _lookup_item(self, com: Any) -> OutlookItem:
        # Only drafts created here may regain ownership after a folder lookup.
        # EntryID alone is insufficient: it must refer to the same store too.
        for owned in self._opened:
            if owned._created and not owned._closed and com.EntryID:
                if (
                    com.EntryID == owned.entry_id
                    and com.Parent.StoreID == owned._com.Parent.StoreID
                ):
                    return owned
        return _wrap_item(com, owner=self)

    @classmethod
    def connect(cls) -> OutlookApp:
        """Attach to running classic Outlook or raise RuntimeError."""
        try:
            com = _require_win32com().GetActiveObject("Outlook.Application")
        except Exception as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("No running classic Outlook instance found.") from exc
        app = cls(com)
        app._validate_profile()
        return app

    @classmethod
    def start(cls, *, exclusive: bool = False) -> OutlookApp:
        """Start/reuse classic Outlook; exclusive=True owns an isolated UAT process.

        A configured profile is required before COM activation. The resulting
        MAPI namespace must also have an active profile and accessible store.
        """
        if not _configured_profiles():
            raise RuntimeError("No configured Outlook MAPI profile; configure a test profile first")
        try:
            com, session = _start_office(
                _require_win32com(),
                "Outlook.Application",
                "OUTLOOK.EXE",
                exclusive=exclusive,
            )
        except _OfficeStartupError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Classic Outlook COM is unavailable; install classic Outlook and "
                "configure a MAPI profile. Exclusive mode requires no existing OUTLOOK.EXE. "
                "New Outlook is not supported by COM."
            ) from exc
        app = cls(com, _session=session)
        try:
            app._validate_profile()
        except BaseException as exc:
            try:
                app.quit()
            except Exception as cleanup_error:
                exc.add_note(f"Office cleanup also failed: {cleanup_error}")
            raise
        return app

    def default_folder(self, name_or_id: str | int = "inbox") -> OutlookFolder:
        """Get inbox/drafts/sent/deleted/calendar or an OlDefaultFolders integer."""
        try:
            folder_id = _FOLDERS[name_or_id.lower()] if isinstance(name_or_id, str) else name_or_id
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown Outlook default folder: {name_or_id}") from exc
        try:
            com = self._namespace.GetDefaultFolder(folder_id)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise LookupError(f"Outlook default folder unavailable: {name_or_id}") from exc
        return OutlookFolder(com, _owner=self)

    def create_mail(self, *, to: str = "", subject: str = "", body: str = "") -> OutlookMail:
        """Create an unsent message; call save() or save_as() to persist it."""
        mail = OutlookMail(self._com.CreateItem(0), _owner=self, _created=True)  # olMailItem
        self._opened.append(mail)
        mail.to, mail.subject, mail.body = to, subject, body
        return mail

    def create_appointment(self, *, subject: str = "") -> OutlookAppointment:
        """Create an unsaved calendar appointment without sending invitations."""
        item = OutlookAppointment(self._com.CreateItem(1), _owner=self, _created=True)
        self._opened.append(item)
        item.subject = subject
        return item

    def open_item(self, path: str | Path) -> OutlookItem:
        """Open a local mail/calendar MSG file; the wrapper owns only this item."""
        try:
            com = self._namespace.OpenSharedItem(str(Path(path).resolve()))
        except Exception as exc:
            raise LookupError(f"Outlook item file unavailable: {path}") from exc
        try:
            item = _wrap_item(com, owner=self)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                com.Close(1)
            except Exception:
                pass
            raise
        self._opened.append(item)
        return item

    def quit(self, *, save_changes: bool = False) -> None:
        """Close owned items; quit/wait for the process only in exclusive mode."""
        failed: list[OutlookItem] = []
        errors: list[str] = []
        for item in self._opened:
            try:
                item.close(save=save_changes)
            except Exception as exc:
                failed.append(item)
                errors.append(str(exc))
        self._opened = failed
        if errors:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not close Outlook items: " + "; ".join(errors))
        if self._session is not None:
            self._session.quit(self._com, release=self._release_com)
        else:
            self._release_com()

    def _release_com(self) -> None:
        for resource in self._resources:
            resource._com = None
        self._resources.clear()
        self._namespace = None
        self._com = None

    def __enter__(self) -> OutlookApp:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_: Any) -> None:
        self.quit()

class OutlookMail(OutlookItem):
    """A mail message with recipients, body and attachment access."""

    def _require_owned_draft(self) -> OutlookApp:
        if self._owner is None or not self._created or self._closed:
            raise PermissionError("Move/delete requires a live draft created by this OutlookApp")
        if self._com.Sent:
            raise PermissionError("Move/delete is restricted to unsent drafts")
        return self._owner

    @property
    def parent_folder(self) -> OutlookFolder:
        """Current containing folder (after save/move), without transferring ownership."""
        return OutlookFolder(self._com.Parent, _owner=self._owner)

    def move(self, folder: OutlookFolder) -> OutlookMail:
        """Move an owned draft and keep this wrapper bound to the returned COM item.

        Only folders obtained from the creating OutlookApp are accepted. Existing
        mailbox items and locally opened MSG files cannot be moved or deleted.
        """
        owner = self._require_owned_draft()
        if not isinstance(folder, OutlookFolder) or folder._owner is not owner:
            raise PermissionError("Destination must belong to the draft's OutlookApp")
        moved = self._com.Move(folder._com)
        if moved is None:
            self._closed = True  # outcome unknown; never reuse a potentially stale proxy
            raise RuntimeError("Outlook Move returned no item; verify the destination folder")
        # The proxy Move() returns is only half alive on PST stores: Delete() on
        # it silently does nothing. Re-fetch the item by its new EntryID so every
        # later operation acts on a proxy Outlook fully honours. If that re-fetch
        # is uncertain (_fresh_item raises), the item has physically moved but we
        # hold no trustworthy handle: invalidate this wrapper so no later
        # move()/delete() touches the stale pre-move proxy, and surface the error.
        try:
            self._com = owner._fresh_item(moved)
        except Exception:
            self._closed = True
            raise
        return self

    def delete(self, *, permanent: bool = False) -> None:
        """Delete an owned draft; permanent deletion requires explicit opt-in.

        Normal deletion moves to that store's Deleted Items folder, retaining
        the returned item for verification/cleanup. Repeated normal deletion
        never silently becomes permanent. permanent=True is allowed only there.
        """
        owner = self._require_owned_draft()
        if not isinstance(permanent, bool):
            raise TypeError("permanent must be a bool")
        parent = self._com.Parent
        deleted = parent.Store.GetDefaultFolder(3)  # olFolderDeletedItems in this store
        in_deleted = parent.EntryID == deleted.EntryID and parent.StoreID == deleted.StoreID
        if permanent:
            if not in_deleted:
                raise ValueError("Permanent deletion requires the draft to be in Deleted Items")
            entry_id, store_id = str(self._com.EntryID), str(parent.StoreID)
            owner._refetch_or_same(self._com).Delete()
            self._closed = True
            if owner._item_still_present(entry_id, store_id):
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "Outlook kept the draft in Deleted Items after Delete(); "
                    "permanent deletion did not take effect"
                )
        else:
            if in_deleted:
                raise ValueError("Draft is already in Deleted Items; use explicit permanent=True")
            self.move(OutlookFolder(deleted, _owner=owner))

    @property
    def to(self) -> str:
        """Semicolon-separated recipient names or addresses."""
        return str(self._com.To)

    @to.setter
    def to(self, value: str) -> None:
        self._com.To = value

    @property
    def cc(self) -> str:
        """Carbon-copy recipients."""
        return str(self._com.CC)

    @cc.setter

        self._com.CC = value

    @property

        self._com.HTMLBody = value

    @property
    def attachment_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of attachments."""
        return int(self._com.Attachments.Count)

    def attachment(self, index: int) -> OutlookAttachment:
        """Return an attachment by 1-based index."""
        return OutlookAttachment(self._com.Attachments.Item(index), _owner=self._owner)

    def add_attachment(self, path: str | Path) -> OutlookAttachment:
        """Attach a local file by value; FileNotFoundError when it does not exist.

        Outlook itself ignores a missing path without raising, which would
        leave the message silently without the attachment.
        """
        resolved = Path(path).resolve()
        if not resolved.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(str(resolved))
        return OutlookAttachment(
            self._com.Attachments.Add(str(resolved), 1),
            _owner=self._owner,
        )

    def send(self) -> None:
        """Explicitly send this message using Outlook's account and security policy.

        No other method sends mail. Object Model Guard may prompt or reject
        this operation; its restrictions are not bypassed.
        """
        self._com.Send()
        self._closed = True

def move(self, folder: OutlookFolder) -> OutlookMail:
    """Move an owned draft and keep this wrapper bound to the returned COM item.

    Only folders obtained from the creating OutlookApp are accepted. Existing
    mailbox items and locally opened MSG files cannot be moved or deleted.
    """
    owner = self._require_owned_draft()
    if not isinstance(folder, OutlookFolder) or folder._owner is not owner:
        raise PermissionError("Destination must belong to the draft's OutlookApp")
    moved = self._com.Move(folder._com)
    if moved is None:
        self._closed = True  # outcome unknown; never reuse a potentially stale proxy
        raise RuntimeError("Outlook Move returned no item; verify the destination folder")
    # The proxy Move() returns is only half alive on PST stores: Delete() on
    # it silently does nothing. Re-fetch the item by its new EntryID so every
    # later operation acts on a proxy Outlook fully honours. If that re-fetch
    # is uncertain (_fresh_item raises), the item has physically moved but we
    # hold no trustworthy handle: invalidate this wrapper so no later
    # move()/delete() touches the stale pre-move proxy, and surface the error.
    try:
        self._com = owner._fresh_item(moved)
    except Exception:
        self._closed = True
        raise
    return self

class OutlookFolder:
    """Outlook folder with 1-based, read-only item lookup."""

    def __init__(self, _com: Any, *, _owner: OutlookApp | None = None) -> None:
        self._com = _com
        self._owner = _owner
        if _owner is not None:
            _owner._resources.append(self)

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Folder display name."""
        return str(self._com.Name)

    @property
    def entry_id(self) -> str:
        """Folder EntryID, unique within its store."""
        return str(self._com.EntryID)

    @property
    def store_id(self) -> str:
        """Containing store's identifier."""
        return str(self._com.StoreID)

    @property
    def item_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of items, including classes outside the mail/calendar API."""
        return int(self._com.Items.Count)

    def item(self, index: int) -> OutlookItem:
        """Return mail/appointment by 1-based index; reject unsupported classes."""
        try:
            com = self._com.Items.Item(index)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise LookupError(f"Outlook item not found at index {index}") from exc
        return self._owner._lookup_item(com) if self._owner is not None else _wrap_item(com)

    def find_item(self, entry_id: str) -> OutlookItem | None:
        """Find mail/appointment by EntryID in this folder; return None when absent."""
        for index in range(1, self.item_count + 1):
            com = self._com.Items.Item(index)
            if com.EntryID == entry_id:
                return self._owner._lookup_item(com) if self._owner is not None else _wrap_item(com)
        return None

    def folder(self, name_or_index: str | int) -> OutlookFolder:
        """Return a subfolder by name or 1-based index."""
        try:
            com = self._com.Folders.Item(name_or_index)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise LookupError(f"Outlook folder not found: {name_or_index}") from exc
        return OutlookFolder(com, _owner=self._owner)

Facade over an Oracle Forms Java client.

Built by :meth:Desktop.launch_oracle_forms (or :meth:Desktop.attach_oracle_forms). Wraps the underlying :class:Application process and exposes Forms-native selectors (block, item, menu, LOV) plus function-key shortcuts.

docs.title: function_key
docs.text:
function_key(key: str) -> None

Send an Oracle-Forms function-key shortcut to the form window.

key is either an :class:OracleFormsKey attribute value ("F7", "Shift+F5" …) or any raw key spec accepted by :func:_translate_key.

The delivery mechanism is layered — most reliable first:

  1. JAB focus request for the top-level accessible context so Swing's InputMap sees the JFrame as focused. Otherwise the WHEN_IN_FOCUSED_WINDOW binding does not fire when the OS keyboard focus lives in another window.
  2. PostMessage(WM_KEYDOWN) to the Java HWND. Delivers to the JVM's WndProc without needing OS foreground focus. Unmodified keys only — PostMessage cannot set the target thread's modifier state.
  3. bring_to_foreground + global SendInput for modifier combos and for hosts that filter PostMessage keys entirely.

docs.title: wait_for_status
docs.text:
wait_for_status(needle: str, *, timeout: float = 5.0, poll_interval: float = 0.1) -> str

Block until the status line contains needle, then return it.

Preferred over sleep(x); assert needle in app.status_line() — a PostMessage-delivered function key is scheduled on the Swing event dispatch thread, so the status text lags the API call by an unpredictable interval. This poll avoids both flakiness and wasted wait time in the fast path.

Empty needle is rejected — "" in any_string is universally True, so wait_for_status("") would return immediately regardless of the actual status line.

docs.title: status_line
docs.text:
status_line() -> str

Return the current text of the status bar at the bottom of the form.

Looks for a component named StatusLine (the dolphin convention + the Swing mock) and returns its accessible description — which the form's programme is expected to keep in sync with the visible status text via AccessibleContext.setAccessibleDescription.

Falls back to role-based lookups (JAB role "status bar") and, as a last resort, any label whose accessible name matches the Record N of M regex.

docs.title: bring_to_foreground
docs.text:
bring_to_foreground() -> None

Force the Java window to the foreground so keyboard replay works.

pywinauto's send_keys uses global SendInput which requires the target window to have foreground focus. Java Swing windows on Windows tend to lose focus quickly after launch — call this before any :meth:OracleFormsItem.type_text / :meth:function_key sequence in headless/CI environments.

Uses the well-known AttachThreadInput trick to bypass Windows' foreground-lock: a background thread cannot call SetForegroundWindow unless it is attached to the currently- foreground thread's input queue.

docs.title: OracleFormsKey
docs.text:
Mnemonic constants for the Oracle Forms function-key contract.

Attributes are the shortcut names understood by :func:OracleFormsApp.function_key and by pywinauto's type_keys escape sequence ({F7}, {F8}, +{F7}…).

.. warning::

This table is an all-or-nothing choice, not a list of independent constants. The Forms runtime loads exactly one key-binding resource file, and every key comes from that one file. These values follow the PC-style family (fmrpcweb.res). A host running the stock fmrweb.res uses a different family, and mixing entries from the two is worse than picking the wrong one wholesale — on a stock-file host these bindings mean:

  • DUPLICATE_RECORD → Exit, discarding uncommitted changes
  • INSERT_RECORD → Clear Record
  • DELETE_RECORD → Duplicate Record
  • CLEAR_FORM → Next Primary Key

Before relying on these, open the form and press Ctrl+K ("Show Keys") to see the bindings your runtime actually loaded. If they do not match, override the whole block rather than individual entries.

Entries marked unverified below are consistent with the PC-style family but have not been confirmed against a published resource file.

docs.title: Playwright compatibility layer
docs.text:
Playwright-shaped facade over dolphin's CDP session. Use to migrate existing Playwright tests to Electron / CEF targets that dolphin handles better.

Playwright-shaped API on top of :class:CDPSession.

Ease migration for teams with existing Playwright tests. Import dolphin_desktop.playwright_compat as if it were playwright.sync_api and drive an Electron / CEF app through the same call shapes:

from dolphin_desktop.playwright_compat import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
    page = browser.contexts[0].pages[0]
    page.locator("#login").click()
    page.locator("input[name=user]").fill("alice")
    page.locator("button[type=submit]").click()
    assert page.locator(".welcome").is_visible()

The mapping is deliberately thin — every attribute forwards to the underlying dolphin object. Anything Playwright-specific that dolphin does not implement (video recording, tracing viewer, remote grid bridge) raises :class:NotImplementedError with a pointer to the dolphin equivalent.

Not a drop-in for playwright.async_api — dolphin's CDP surface is sync-only. If your tests are async, use Playwright directly and switch to dolphin only for the desktop pieces Playwright cannot reach.

Timeouts

Every timeout= parameter in this module is in milliseconds, exactly like Playwright — page.goto(url, timeout=60000) waits 60 seconds and locator.wait_for(timeout=5000) waits 5 seconds. This differs from the native dolphin API (:class:dolphin_desktop.CDPSession, :class:dolphin_desktop.Locator), where timeouts are seconds. Mixing the two in one test file is the usual source of confusion: the rule is that anything reached through playwright_compat speaks milliseconds.

Known divergences

The shim covers the call shapes most migrations hit, not all of Playwright. These differ and will not be silently papered over:

  • locator.fill(value) — Playwright names the parameter value; here it is text. Positional calls work either way.
  • locator.is_visible() / is_enabled() / is_checked() accept timeout= for call compatibility but ignore it — the underlying :class:CDPLocator state readers are non-blocking and have no timeout.
  • locator.count() and locator.all_text_contents() take no timeout, exactly as in Playwright.
  • page.keyboard_press(key) — there is no page.keyboard object, so Playwright's page.keyboard.press(key) has no equivalent shape.
  • sync_playwright() is a context manager only; Playwright's p = sync_playwright().start() form is unsupported.
  • page.screenshot() returns a PIL Image, not bytes, and its path argument is positional.
  • Not implemented at all: locator.all(), check()/uncheck(), select_option(), set_input_files(), page.go_back() / go_forward(), context.new_page(), context.storage_state(), context.tracing, page.video, and the expect() assertion library. Use the native :class:CDPLocator surface or Dolphin's own trace/video facilities for these — it reaches everything the shim does not.

docs.title: sync_playwright
docs.text:
sync_playwright() -> Iterator[_Playwright]

Yield a Playwright-shaped facade backed by dolphin's CDP session.

Usage matches Playwright's own sync_playwright context manager::

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
    page = browser.contexts[0].pages[0]
    page.locator("#login").click()
    browser.close()

docs.title: async_playwright
docs.text:
async_playwright() -> NoReturn

Reject Playwright's asynchronous API explicitly.

Dolphin's compatibility layer is synchronous. Raising here gives users a deterministic migration hint instead of an import-time ImportError.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from dolphin_desktop.playwright_compat import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
    page = browser.contexts[0].pages[0]
    page.locator("#login").click()
    page.locator("input[name=user]").fill("alice")
    page.locator("button[type=submit]").click()
    assert page.locator(".welcome").is_visible()
    browser.close()

docs.title: Next to an existing session
docs.text:
The facade can attach to an app that dolphin already drives, on the same thread, for example one started with Desktop().launch_electron_cdp(...):

from dolphin_desktop import Desktop
from dolphin_desktop.playwright_compat import sync_playwright

app, session = Desktop().launch_electron_cdp("app.exe", debug_port=9222)
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
    page = browser.contexts[0].pages[0]
    assert page.title()
    browser.close()          # disconnects the facade only
session.locator("#ready").wait_for()   # the first session still works
session.close()

All CDP sessions on one thread share a single Playwright driver, because Playwright's sync API allows only one running instance per thread. Each session still has its own CDP connection, so closing one never disconnects another. The driver stops when the last session on the thread closes. Close every session (or use it as a context manager) on the thread that opened it, before that thread ends: a session left open keeps the driver, a node process, running until it is closed or garbage collected. Playwright objects only work on the thread that created them, so close() from any other thread raises DolphinError and leaves the session open for its owner to close.

docs.title: Not implemented
docs.text:
The following Playwright APIs are not available through the compat layer — dolphin does not have equivalents:

  • Firefox / WebKit browser types (dolphin is Chromium-only).
  • chromium.launch() — dolphin never spawns a standalone Chromium; use Desktop().launch_electron_cdp(...) for Electron apps or connect_over_cdp(url) for a running one.
  • Async API (async_playwright) — dolphin's CDP surface is sync-only; calling it raises NotImplementedError with a migration hint.
  • Trace viewer / video recording APIs — dolphin has its own trace / video capture (see the pytest plugin options).
  • Multi-context / storage-state persistence — Electron apps run under a single default context.

Calls to these attributes raise NotImplementedError with a pointer to the dolphin equivalent.

The same explicit exception is used for browser.new_context(), context.new_page(), context.storage_state(), context.tracing and page.video. These names are exposed so an accidentally ported Playwright test fails with a useful compatibility message rather than an AttributeError.

docs.title: pytest Plugin
docs.text: Dolphin registers a pytest plugin automatically through the pytest11 package entry point. Install dolphin-desktop in the same environment as pytest; no import is required in conftest.py.

docs.text:
def test_example(launch):
    app = launch("notepad.exe")
    win = app.window(class_name="Notepad")
    ...

Function-scoped helper. It calls Desktop.launch(...), records the returned Application, and calls Application.kill() during teardown.

launch accepts the same keyword arguments as Desktop.launch:

def test_with_args(launch):
    app = launch("myapp.exe", timeout=20, startup_delay=1.0)
    win = app.window(title="My App")

docs.title: dolphin_backend
docs.text:
def test_backend_name(dolphin_backend):
    assert isinstance(dolphin_backend, str)

Session-scoped value of --dolphin-backend. Accepts registered backend IDs, including installed dolphin_desktop.backends entry points and backends registered with register_backend() while loading conftest.py, plus auto. Final validation runs after collection, so nested conftest.py files discovered under the selected test paths can register backends before validation. Unknown IDs produce a pytest usage error listing registered backends; there is no fallback. Validation does not construct backends or check optional dependencies. The desktop fixture passes the selected ID to Desktop; backend capabilities and stack-specific launch requirements still apply. Native Desktop.launch() and connect() use pywinauto; external providers can be called through the public resolve_backend(dolphin_backend) API. With auto, dolphin_backend retains the requested string, while Desktop resolves it once during construction (uia on Windows) and uses that concrete backend for launch(), connect() and capability queries.

docs.title: Per-Test Marker
docs.text:
Use @pytest.mark.dolphin(...) for per-test overrides:

import pytest


@pytest.mark.dolphin(timeout=30, video_mode="keepall")
def test_slow_flow(launch):
    app = launch("myapp.exe")

@pytest.mark.dolphin(headless=True) skips the test unless headless mode is active.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Dolphin logging accepts only DEBUG, INFO, and ERROR; the default is INFO. --dolphin-desktop-log-level is validated by pytest, while config(log_level=...) raises ValueError for any other value without changing the configured defaults or logger state. The same three values are accepted case-insensitively by the Python API.

For environment configuration, DOLPHIN_DESKTOP_LOG_LEVEL takes precedence over DOLPHIN_LOG_LEVEL. The selected value is validated after precedence is resolved; an invalid value emits a warning and falls back safely to INFO, even when the lower-priority variable is valid.

In standalone use, setup_logging() owns one console handler on the dolphin_desktop logger and repeated calls reuse it. Under pytest, pytest owns the handlers: Dolphin installs none on its logger, leaves propagation enabled, and applies the level/redaction configuration so messages reach pytest's handlers without duplicate output.

--dolphin-screenshot-on-fail is diagnostic support and must not change the test result. If the screenshot backend cannot capture an image (for example, because the desktop is locked or ImageGrab raises), Dolphin logs a warning and preserves the original test exception and exit status. It does not emit a pytest INTERNALERROR caused by the failed capture.

The JUnit/XML, fallback HTML, pytest stdout/stderr and diagnostic log remain available for investigating the failure. A successful capture is written under dolphin-screenshots/ and its path is included in the test report; a failed capture does not create a misleading or partial PNG.

docs.title: SAP GUI for Windows
docs.text: SAP GUI automation via SAP GUI Scripting COM. Requires SAP GUI for Windows with scripting enabled.

docs.title: SapGui
docs.text:
Entry point for SAP GUI for Windows automation.

This wrapper attaches to the SAP GUI Scripting engine exposed by a running SAP GUI for Windows process. SAP GUI Scripting must be enabled in the SAP client and allowed by the target SAP system.

Source code in src\dolphin_desktop\_sap.py 
class SapGui:
    """Entry point for SAP GUI for Windows automation.

    This wrapper attaches to the SAP GUI Scripting engine exposed by a running
    SAP GUI for Windows process. SAP GUI Scripting must be enabled in the SAP
    client and allowed by the target SAP system.
    """

    #: Fronts the SapBackend (SAP GUI Scripting COM stack).
    backend_id: str = "sap"

    @classmethod
    def backend(cls):
        from ._backend import resolve as _resolve

        return _resolve(cls.backend_id)

    @classmethod
    def backend_supports(cls, capability) -> bool:
        return cls.backend().supports(capability)

    @classmethod
    def require_capability(cls, capability) -> None:
        cls.backend().require_capability(capability)

    def __init__(self, _com: Any) -> None:
        self._com = _com

    @classmethod
    def connect(cls, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> SapGui:
        seconds, end = _deadline(timeout)
        last_exc: Exception | None = None

        while True:
            try:
                client = _require_win32com()
                sap_gui = client.GetObject(_SAPGUI_PROG_ID)
                return cls(_get_scripting_engine(sap_gui))
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exc = exc
                if time.monotonic() >= end:
                    raise ApplicationError(
                        "Could not connect to SAP GUI Scripting engine after "
                        f"{seconds:g}s. Ensure SAP GUI for Windows is running and "
                        "SAP GUI Scripting is enabled on both the client and SAP system."
                    ) from last_exc
                _sleep()

    @property
    def raw(self) -> Any:
        return self._com

    @staticmethod
    def scripting_security_handler() -> threading.Event:
        """Start a background thread that auto-dismisses SAP GUI Scripting security dialogs.

        Only the SAP GUI security-notification dialog is touched: the
        window must belong to a SAP front-end process, carry the standard
        dialog class, and name SAP GUI in its caption. Dialogs from any
        other application on the desktop are left alone.

        Returns a stop event — call ``stop_event.set()`` when done.
        """
        stop_event = threading.Event()
        t = threading.Thread(
            target=_scripting_security_worker,
            args=(stop_event,),
            daemon=True,
        )
        t.start()
        return stop_event

    @staticmethod
    def is_server_reachable(
        host: str = "127.0.0.1",
        port: int = 3200,
        *,
        timeout: float = 3.0,
    ) -> bool:
        """Return True when the SAP application server is reachable on *host*:*port*.

        Uses a raw TCP connect so no SAP GUI process needs to be running yet.
        Typical usage in a test::

            if not SapGui.is_server_reachable():
                pytest.skip("SAP server unavailable")
        """
        import socket as _socket

        try:
            with _socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
                return True
        except OSError:
            return False

    def wait_for_any_connection(self, timeout: float = 30.0) -> None:
        """Wait until at least one connection appears in the SAP GUI engine.

        ``keyboard_login()`` submits credentials but the SAP session registers
        in the scripting engine only after the server processes the login —
        an inherently asynchronous step.  Without this method every test that
        uses keyboard login must poll ``connections()`` with a raw
        ``time.monotonic()`` deadline, forcing a stdlib ``time`` import into
        test files that should only depend on dolphin_desktop.
        """
        seconds, end = _deadline(timeout)
        while True:
            if self.connections():
                return
            if time.monotonic() >= end:
                raise WaitTimeoutError(f"No SAP connection appeared after {seconds:g}s")
            _sleep()

    @staticmethod
    def keyboard_login(win_title: str, user: str, password: str) -> None:
        """Fill SAP login credentials without mouse movement, then press Enter.

        The User field must initially have focus and expose the SAP automation
        ID ``RSYST-BNAME``, ``txtRSYST-BNAME`` or ``ctxtRSYST-BNAME`` (optionally
        in a component path). UIA must expose exactly one password Edit control.
        Both fields must have writable Value patterns.
        Credentials are set literally on those controls, never sent as global
        keystrokes. Unsupported controls or lost focus abort the login; use SAP
        GUI Scripting instead when the login screen lacks these UIA patterns.

        Raises:
            ValueError: A credential contains a control character.
            ApplicationError: The window, fields or focus cannot be verified.
        """
        # Validate both values before connecting or sending any input. In a
        # single-line login field tabs/newlines must not navigate or disappear.
        for value in (user, password):
            if any(ord(char) < 32 or 127 <= ord(char) <= 159 for char in value):
                raise ValueError("SAP login credentials cannot contain control characters")
        try:
            from pywinauto import Application as _PwApp
            from pywinauto.keyboard import send_keys as _send_keys
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise ApplicationError("pywinauto not available") from exc

        app = _PwApp(backend="uia")
        try:
            app.connect(title=win_title, timeout=15)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise ApplicationError(f"Cannot connect to '{win_title}': {exc}") from exc

        try:
            dlg = app.window(title=win_title).wrapper_object()
            dlg.set_focus()
            time.sleep(1.0)
            fields = dlg.descendants(control_type="Edit")
            users = [
                field
                for field in fields
                if field.element_info.automation_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
                in {"RSYST-BNAME", "txtRSYST-BNAME", "ctxtRSYST-BNAME"}
                and not field.element_info.element.CurrentIsPassword
            ]
            passwords = [field for field in fields if field.element_info.element.CurrentIsPassword]
            if len(users) != 1 or len(passwords) != 1:
                raise ApplicationError("Cannot verify SAP login fields")
            user_field, password_field = users[0], passwords[0]
            # Resolve both patterns before changing either field. Calling
            # set_edit_text would also log the credential in pywinauto.
            user_value = user_field.iface_value
            password_value = password_field.iface_value
            if user_value.CurrentIsReadOnly or password_value.CurrentIsReadOnly:
                raise ApplicationError("SAP login fields are read-only")

            def fill(field: Any, pattern: Any, text: str) -> None:
                def verify() -> None:
                    if not field.has_keyboard_focus() or (
                        field is password_field and not field.element_info.element.CurrentIsPassword
                    ):
                        raise ApplicationError("SAP login focus changed; login aborted")

                verify()
                # One targeted write cannot redirect any part of the credential
                # even if focus changes between the check and SetValue.
                pattern.SetValue(text)
                verify()

            fill(user_field, user_value, user)
            _send_keys("{TAB}")
            time.sleep(0.1)
            fill(password_field, password_value, password)
            _send_keys("{ENTER}")
            return
        except Exception:
            # Provider errors may contain the SetValue argument. Leave the
            # handler before raising so the safe error has no secret context.
            pass
        raise ApplicationError("Cannot safely complete SAP login; fields or focus unavailable")

    def connection(self, index: int = 0) -> SapConnection:
        """Return a SAP GUI connection by zero-based index."""
        return SapConnection(_collection_item(self._com.Children, index))

    def connections(self) -> list[SapConnection]:
        count = _collection_count(self._com.Children)
        if count is None:
            return []
        return [self.connection(index) for index in range(count)]

    def close_all_connections(self) -> None:
        try:
            n = self._com.Children.Count
        except Exception:
            return
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            try:
                self._com.Children(i).CloseConnection()
            except Exception:
                pass

    def open_connection(self, name: str, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> SapSession | None:
        """Open a named SAP system connection.

        Calls ``GuiApplication.OpenConnection`` (sync) so the SAP login window
        appears before this method returns.  If the scripting session is
        accessible (server-side scripting enabled), returns the
        :class:`SapSession`; otherwise returns ``None`` so the caller can fall
        back to keyboard / UIA login.
        """
        com_conn = self._com.OpenConnection(name, True)
        _, end = _deadline(timeout or 10.0)
        while True:
            # Try the returned connection's children first.
            try:
                return SapSession(_collection_item(com_conn.Children, 0))
            except Exception:
                pass
            # Fallback: scan all engine connections.
            try:
                n = self._com.Children.Count
                for i in range(n):
                    try:
                        return SapSession(_collection_item(self._com.Children(i).Children, 0))
                    except Exception:
                        continue
            except Exception:
                pass
            if time.monotonic() >= end:
                # Scripting session not accessible — caller should use UIA/keyboard.
                return None
            _sleep()

    def session(self, *, connection: int = 0, session: int = 0) -> SapSession:
        """Return a SAP GUI session by zero-based connection and session index."""
        return self.connection(connection).session(session)

    @property
    def version(self) -> str:
        try:
            return str(self._com.Version)
        except Exception:
            return ""

    try:
        app.connect(title=win_title, timeout=15)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ApplicationError(f"Cannot connect to '{win_title}': {exc}") from exc

    try:
        dlg = app.window(title=win_title).wrapper_object()
        dlg.set_focus()
        time.sleep(1.0)
        fields = dlg.descendants(control_type="Edit")
        users = [
            field
            for field in fields
            if field.element_info.automation_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
            in {"RSYST-BNAME", "txtRSYST-BNAME", "ctxtRSYST-BNAME"}
            and not field.element_info.element.CurrentIsPassword
        ]
        passwords = [field for field in fields if field.element_info.element.CurrentIsPassword]
        if len(users) != 1 or len(passwords) != 1:
            raise ApplicationError("Cannot verify SAP login fields")
        user_field, password_field = users[0], passwords[0]
        # Resolve both patterns before changing either field. Calling
        # set_edit_text would also log the credential in pywinauto.
        user_value = user_field.iface_value
        password_value = password_field.iface_value
        if user_value.CurrentIsReadOnly or password_value.CurrentIsReadOnly:
            raise ApplicationError("SAP login fields are read-only")

        def fill(field: Any, pattern: Any, text: str) -> None:
            def verify() -> None:
                if not field.has_keyboard_focus() or (
                    field is password_field and not field.element_info.element.CurrentIsPassword
                ):
                    raise ApplicationError("SAP login focus changed; login aborted")

            verify()
            # One targeted write cannot redirect any part of the credential
            # even if focus changes between the check and SetValue.
            pattern.SetValue(text)
            verify()

        fill(user_field, user_value, user)
        _send_keys("{TAB}")
        time.sleep(0.1)
        fill(password_field, password_value, password)
        _send_keys("{ENTER}")
        return
    except Exception:
        # Provider errors may contain the SetValue argument. Leave the
        # handler before raising so the safe error has no secret context.
        pass
    raise ApplicationError("Cannot safely complete SAP login; fields or focus unavailable")

def open_connection(self, name: str, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> SapSession | None:
    """Open a named SAP system connection.

    Calls ``GuiApplication.OpenConnection`` (sync) so the SAP login window
    appears before this method returns.  If the scripting session is
    accessible (server-side scripting enabled), returns the
    :class:`SapSession`; otherwise returns ``None`` so the caller can fall
    back to keyboard / UIA login.
    """
    com_conn = self._com.OpenConnection(name, True)
    _, end = _deadline(timeout or 10.0)
    while True:
        # Try the returned connection's children first.
        try:
            return SapSession(_collection_item(com_conn.Children, 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        # Fallback: scan all engine connections.
        try:
            n = self._com.Children.Count
            for i in range(n):
                try:
                    return SapSession(_collection_item(self._com.Children(i).Children, 0))
                except Exception:
                    continue
        except Exception:
            pass
        if time.monotonic() >= end:
            # Scripting session not accessible — caller should use UIA/keyboard.
            return None
        _sleep()

class SapConnection:
    """Wrapper around a SAP GUI Scripting connection."""

    def __init__(self, _com: Any) -> None:
        self._com = _com

    @property
    def raw(self) -> Any:
        return self._com

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        """Return the connection description (SAP system name / instance)."""
        try:
            return str(self._com.Description)
        except Exception:
            return ""

    def close(self) -> None:
        try:
            self._com.CloseConnection()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def session(self, index: int = 0) -> SapSession:
        """Return a session from this connection by zero-based index."""
        return SapSession(_collection_item(self._com.Children, index))

    def sessions(self) -> list[SapSession]:
        count = _collection_count(self._com.Children)
        if count is None:
            return []
        return [self.session(index) for index in range(count)]

    def wait_for_session_count(self, expected: int, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Wait until this connection has exactly *expected* sessions.

        SAP GUI Scripting's CreateSession() and the /i command that closes a
        session are asynchronous — the Children collection does not update
        synchronously with the call.  Without this method every test that opens
        or closes a session is forced to sprinkle raw time.sleep() calls and
        import the stdlib time module just to paper over the race.  Keeping the
        poll here lets tests express intent ("wait until there are N sessions")
        instead of "sleep and hope", and ensures the wait uses the same
        configurable poll interval as every other dolphin_desktop wait helper.
        """
        seconds, end = _deadline(timeout)
        while True:
            if len(self.sessions()) == expected:
                return
            if time.monotonic() >= end:
                raise WaitTimeoutError(
                    f"Session count did not reach {expected} after {seconds:g}s; "
                    f"current={len(self.sessions())}"
                )
            _sleep()

    def create_session(self) -> None:
        """Request a new SAP session on this connection.

        The new session appears asynchronously in the connection's session
        list.  Pair with ``wait_for_session_count`` to block until it is
        accessible::

            n = len(conn.sessions())
            conn.create_session()
            conn.wait_for_session_count(n + 1)
            new_sess = conn.session(n)
        """
        try:
            sess_com = _collection_item(self._com.Children, 0)
            if not _call_first(sess_com, ("CreateSession", "createSession")):
                raise ApplicationError("SAP session does not expose CreateSession")
        except ApplicationError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            raise ApplicationError(f"Cannot create new SAP session: {exc}") from exc
